News.title: ‘Our noise is to win games’; Enzo Maresca challenges Man City to continue winning mentality
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Enzo Maresca declared that Manchester City brought their own noise to Anfield after they won 3-0 in front of a hostile Liverpool crowd in their first game since being found guilty of 114 Premier League charges.

And the City manager has challenged his team to carry on silencing opposition crowds by winning.

The Liverpool supporters called City cheats in a series of chants but Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scored as Maresca’s team maintained their 100 percent start to the Premier League season.

City still face potential punishments including expulsion from the top flight or a points penalty that could result in relegation.

open image in gallery Enzo Maresca praised his Man City players following their 3-0 win at Anfield ( PA )

But Maresca’s team shrugged that off to record their joint biggest Premier League win at Anfield.

And the Italian said: "It was not easy for the players after the last two or three weeks but they dealt with the situation very well. I said during the week we need to learn how to deal with the outside noise because of the situation. The noise will always be there so we need to learn how to deal with that but at the same time we need to try and bring our noise, which is win games which is what we have done today.

"At the end of the game, our fans were singing so the noise was from us and not the environment. All the away games are going to be with noise so we need to learn how to deal with the noise. And at the same time, we need to make our noise. Our noise is we're singing at the end, our fans, and this has to be our target at the moment."

News.title: Max Verstappen is back and Mercedes are already worried
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli, third: “It was a very tough race out there but really happy with a podium at the end, I managed to take advantage of the fight between Lewis and Lando. To take P3 is a great result from the team, very happy with that.”

He is told that he can clinch the title at the next race:

“Can I, really? Let’s not worry about that. Let’s try to do the best weekend possible and finish the job.”

Charles Leclerc, second: “We were quite strong at the beginning of the race and then we started degrading at the end of the first stint. I pushed a lot at the beginning of the last stint and then degraded a bit more than the others. I gave it all and I don’t regret anything.

“I don’t think there’s anything more we could do but be a bit more aggressive at the start. It’s true that we brought some small new parts to the car which maybe helped us to do a little step forward but it’s enough. Today I think we had a good pace overall.”

Max Verstappen, winner: “It’s taken a while but I think this race was very good. We had pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyre and the medium. Very happy to win here. You always try to do your best and luckily [the start] it was just good enough.

“I think the last few races have been really positive for us. It’s great to see and we have a lot of motivation in the team to try to deliver even more results... hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year.”

News.title: The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool
News.content:
Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

News.title: Three tasks to get your home ready for autumn, according to a professional cleaner
News.content:
When I was sweating away this summer, I never thought the weather would turn, but it’s almost time to crank up our radiators and crack out the big duvet.

They’re the tasks no one likes doing, but luckily for you, I’ve worked as a cleaner for more than a decade. I’ve discovered some shortcuts to make the hated jobs that bit easier.

Tip one: Keep your summer duvet fresh in storage

If, like me, you want to get your winter duvet out, your summer one needs to be cleaned and packed away to keep it fresh come spring.

Start by spot cleaning any stains. You can just use a standard household fabric stain remover for this. If you want to wash your duvet, most domestic washing machines aren’t big enough to fit a double, let alone a king or a super king. Your best bet is to take them down to the laundrette and follow the care instructions on the label.

News.title: Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs
News.content:
The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”

News.title: Guimaraes looks a £75m bargain as ‘super sub’ makes difference
News.content:
Before the game we talked about two things, the challenge ahead against a team that had not lost in the Premier League. They full deserved to be where they are and it was going to be really tough. The second was to restore our identity and be ourselves again.

We weren’t pleased with our performance against Brighton and we wanted to put it right. But the context is that this was a difficult one [opponent]. But we reacted in a way that was unique and made it so special.

[Leeds] are very well organised, very physical and very committed in everything that they do. They are a threat. They are incredible the way they attack the ball and set-pieces, with belief. They came close to punishing us. They have individual quality and they are in a good moment.

When you play at 12.30 at home and you go one-nil down there’s a lot to do. You have to restore a lot of things. Energy is one of them. We had an incredible response. The crowd changed. You could see it.

We brought a lot of leadership on [with his three subs]. We brought goal threat, to win duels, people who can play forward and penetrate against their high press.

The timing, movement and execution of it [the winning goal], yes, it was a beauty.

News.title: Resurgent Verstappen on fire in the Singapore smog
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix from the Marina Bay Circuit. Given the way the championship standings are, it looks like Kimi Antonelli has one hand on the drivers’ title. That means that the most significant thing is the battle for individual race victories. That includes grands prix, but also sprint races, like we have today.

Formula One is very keen on sprint races, increasing their number significantly next year, but we have never had one in Singapore before. We will find out today whether there was good reason for it. I suppose the logic is that even a processional sprint race is better than a free practice session and that having two qualifying sessions on a street circuit such as this is exciting, too.

Still, although he might be strolling towards the championship, he and Mercedes are not the dominant force they were at the start of the season when he won five in a row having finished second in the opening race. In fact, in the last 10 grands prix, Antonelli has won three and Russell two. With Max Verstappen’s win in Malaysia last weekend it meant each of Red Bull, McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes have won races this season.

It is Verstappen who is in strong form in an upgraded Red Bull, as he snuck pole position from George Russell by just over a tenth of a second. He was followed by Charles Leclerc in the Ferrari and then Oscar Piastri in the McLaren. Antonelli, in the upgraded Mercedes, found things more difficult, finishing down in seventh nearly 0.7sec off the pace.

Anyway, the sprint gets under way in about 30 minutes and we will be here for all the updates from that, as well as qualifying later today.

News.title: Majestic All Blacks copy Springbok playbook to dismantle Australia
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Bledisloe Cup Test as New Zealand host Australia at Eden Park in Auckland.

The All Blacks are enduring one of the toughest periods in their history, having suffered three successive Test defeats against South Africa in August and September, which saw the Springboks claim the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series tour. Dave Rennie’s men are under immense pressure to avoid a fourth consecutive Test defeat for the first time since 1998.

You could argue there’s never been a better opportunity for Australia to beat New Zealand at Eden Park. The Wallabies are enjoying a six-Test unbeaten run – their longest such streak since 2017, with five games in this rejuvenated period coming under new head coach Les Kiss. In their most recent outing, Australia secured an extraordinary 42-38 victory over a much-changed South Africa side in Perth, despite being reduced to 11 players at one point.

Australia will feel further encouraged due to several key absences for New Zealand, as Ardie Savea, Ruben Love, Richie Mo’unga, Caleb Clarke, Fehi Fineanganofo, Billy Proctor and Anton Lienert-Brown are all out injured. In a reshuffle for the All Blacks, Damian McKenzie will begin at fly-half for the first time in 2026. Other notable inclusions for the home side see all three Barrett brothers, Codie Taylor, Tupou Vaa’i, Cam Roigard and Will Jordan starting.

Meanwhile, the visitors are without the suspended Hunter Paisami, with Isaac Henry taking his place at centre. The likes of Ryan Lonergan, Len Ikitau, Harry Wilson, Ben Donaldson and Max Jorgensen, who were all key to the triumph against the Springboks, retain their starting spots.

All the statistics overwhelmingly favour New Zealand. The All Blacks have not lost any edition of the Bledisloe Cup since 2002, winning 51 series to Australia’s 12, and are unbeaten at Eden Park since 1994, when they lost to France. Australia are winless at Eden Park since 1986, tasting defeat there 30 times in 34 games, and have lost their last 11 Tests against New Zealand.

However, given the landscape heading into this historic rivalry between these two heavyweights, it genuinely feels like anything could happen.

Kick-off is at 7:10am.

News.title: Black British Business Awards 2026 winners revealed
News.content:
The chief executive of Dr. Martens has been named the Black British Business Person of the Year at the 2026 Black British Business Awards (BBBAwards).

Ije Nwokorie, who became chief of Dr. Martens in January last year and is the only black chief executive in the FTSE 250, was awarded in recognition of his role shaping Dr. Martens’ growth strategy.

He is recognised inside Dr. Martens for his strong communication with staff, according to the judges.

Before joining Dr. Martens, Mr Nwokorie spent more than 11 years at Wolff Olins, the marketing giant, before working as a senior director at Apple.

Born in the US but brought up from age six against the backdrop of post-civil-war Nigeria, Mr Nwokorie has described how he and his family went from the lifestyle trappings of 1960s America to a small Nigerian village and a home with no running water.

On winning the award, Mr Nwokorie said: “This recognition means a lot to me. While this award bears my name, it reflects the talent, dedication and generosity of the incredible teammates, mentors and leaders who have shaped me as a person and a professional.

“It is a powerful reminder that there is nothing more important in our leadership journeys than the time we invest to help others thrive.”

Alongside his executive career, he has served as a trustee at Charity: water for nearly a decade and held board roles at cultural and humanitarian organisations including the Institute of International Visual Arts and Malaria No More UK.

He also served as chairman of trustees for the Chineke! Orchestra, a British orchestra championing change and the first in Europe to feature a majority of black and ethnically diverse musicians.

The Black British Business Awards started in 2014 to celebrate the achievements of black people in British business. The Telegraph is the national media partner for the awards.

Mr Nwokorie was presented with the award at an exclusive ceremony sponsored by JPMorgan Chase at London’s Hilton Park Lane hotel.

Speaking at the ceremony, Sophie Chandauka, the executive founder of the awards, said: “You lend the BBBAwards credibility not simply to celebrate excellence, but to ensure the best and brightest from all communities get a fair shot. That commitment has made the BBBAwards the UK’s premium awards programme for black business achievement.”

A spokesman for JPMorgan Chase said: “We couldn’t be prouder to support and celebrate such an outstanding breadth of black British talent.

“Their accomplishments continue to inspire future generations and demonstrate the exceptional value they bring to businesses, communities and the wider UK economy.”

This year’s winners are as follows:

Black British Business Person of the Year: Ije Nwokorie, chief executive of Dr Martens

Arts and Media Rising Star: Sheniece Charway, artist partnership manager [EMEA], YouTube/Google

Arts and Media Senior Leader: Amie Parker-Williams, director, digital commissioning and production, Paramount

Fashion, Beauty and Consumer Senior Leader: Andrea Thompson, journalist, brand consultant and former editor-in-chief, Marie Claire UK

Fashion, Beauty and Consumer Rising Star: Yasmin O’Neal, senior director for global brand and impact, DECIEM

Entrepreneur Rising Star: Dr Elsa Zekeng, founder and chief executive, SökerData

Entrepreneur Senior Leader: Antonia Okonma Shittu, founder and chief executive, A-List Lace Hair

Financial Services Rising Star: Nana Agyemang, proposition delivery manager, Barclays

Financial Services Senior Leader: Melissa Max-Macarthy, formerly managing director, head of strategy and innovation, retail banking, NatWest Group

Professional Services Rising Star: Jack Van Cooten, senior manager – external vendors and data, Oliver Wyman

Professional Services Senior Leader: Laurie-Anne Power KC, barrister, 25 Bedford Row

Retail and Hospitality Senior Leader: Leona De Graft, vice-president of global ecommerce, Levi Strauss and Co

Retail and Hospitality Rising Star: Rickey Devonish, head of apprenticeships and emerging talent, JD Group

STEM Rising Star: Maciah Smith, innovation and strategic technology roadmapping analyst, Johnson Matthey

STEM Senior Leader: Eustace Xavier, finance director, technical services, Mitie PLC

Sports.title: ‘This is really bad for the Premier League’ – Man Utd icon Gary Neville fears for football as City batter Liverpool
Sports.content:
Next

GARY NEVILLE has warned Manchester City’s ongoing guilty verdict is “really bad for the Premier League” following their stunning win over Liverpool.

The former Manchester United defender admitted he struggled to praise City’s performance without thinking about the uncertainty surrounding the club’s future.



Enzo Maresca’s side thrashed Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield to maintain their perfect start to the Premier League season.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki were all on target after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off in the second half.



But City’s impressive victory came against a dramatic backdrop, after the Etihad club were found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Prem’s financial rules during a nine-season period.

The reigning champions have appealed the decision and are awaiting the outcome, with potentially severe punishments hanging over the club.



And Neville believes the uncertainty is casting a huge shadow over English football.

Speaking on Sky Sports, he said: “To come and win at Anfield is really difficult and we should be eulogising over them without a but or any hesitation.

“But there is that thing in the back of your mind that they’ve done a brilliant job here today.

“They’ve obviously dominated the game in the last 20 minutes from the red card onwards. They’ve dug in.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, Neville’s biggest concern was what could happen if the guilty verdict is upheld in the coming months.

He added: “If these guilty verdicts obviously are confirmed in January, February, that Manchester City are not going to be in the position that they’re in and there’s going to be a huge cloud hanging over the whole league.

“And this is not good for the Premier League right now. That’s what I’ve just recognised today.

“This is really bad for the Premier League and it’s going to continue for a few months.”

City were greeted by a hostile Anfield crowd, with Liverpool supporters displaying banners and chanting about the financial scandal.



But the controversy failed to distract Maresca’s men, who secured their sixth consecutive league victory to move three points clear at the top of the table.

Sports.title: Fans love Man Utd legend Roy Keane’s priceless reaction to learning Hull star missed match because he was ‘TIRED’
Sports.content:
Next

FANS were cracking up at Roy Keane’s reaction to a Hull star being left out of the line-up for being “tired.”

The Manchester United legend joined fellow pundits Micah Richards and Daniel Sturridge in the Sky Sports studio ahead of the Tigers’ clash with Everton on Sunday.



But he was the target of a cheeky joke by host Mark Chapman.

The Super Sunday presenter was giving a squad update ahead of the clash when he explained that Hull talisman Mohamed Belloumi would not be in the starting XI because he was “tired.”



Knowing Keane’s typically dim view of modern players being too soft, Chapman, Richards and Sturridge all went silent and looked towards Keane in anticipation of a wry comment at the Algerian’s expense.

And the former Republic of Ireland star, perhaps aware of his own reputation cracked a cheeky grin while resisting the urge to comment.

The studio burst into laughter at the sight of their co-star trying to hold in his criticism.

And fans found the moment just as amusing, taking to social media to comment on the awkward moment.

One fan wrote: “They are rage baiting Keane.”

And another added: “Roy heard ‘tired’ and immediately requested the player’s running stats.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Belloumi had spent the international break away with Algeria, starting in games against Zambia, Burundi and Niger.

And despite being too worn down by the matches and the travel to start at the MKM Stadium, he managed to make quite the impact from the bench.

The 24-year-old was introduced in the 64th minute in place of Joe Gelhardt, and fired in an equaliser ten minutes later to rescue a point for his side.

Some fans were chuffed for the breakout star, with one replying to the studio’s reaction: “And yet then Belloumi comes on and steals the show. Impact sub – bosh!”



It has been a dream start to his debut campaign in the Premier League.

He has already scored three times and assisted twice in his first six appearances, with only five players having scored more so far in the league.

Sports.title: Burnham to publish ALL details of dealings with Man City amid pressure to come clean over defence of UAE owners
Sports.content:
CITY PROBE Burnham to publish ALL details of dealings with Man City amid pressure to come clean over defence of UAE owners







Next

ANDY Burnham has finally bowed to pressure to publish all his meetings with Man City’s owners following fury at his defence of the UAE tycoons.

The Prime Minister had been feeling the heat to come clean about his dealings after the club was found guilty of widespread cheating.



The PM’s City links go back to 2018 when he attended the opening of a club office in China.

City deny breaking Prem financial rules and have launched an appeal.



Kemi Badenoch had urged him to publish “everything” related to his work with the club as Greater Manchester mayor.

City have been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.



The club maintained their innocence and appealed against the verdict.

Mr Burnham said last month he would be “really concerned” if City’s Abu Dhabi owners sold the club in the wake of the finding, crediting them with being “a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester”.

Downing Street sought to clarify his comments afterwards, saying the Prime Minister was clear the judgment is serious and that where wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the consequences.

Mr Burnham said he would “put out there” everything he had done to work with the club’s owners as mayor in an interview with the Rest is Politics podcast to be released on Monday.



He said that “the football issues are different from the investment issues”.

“But I see now people trying to conflate these things. I’ve been asked by the leader of the opposition to publish details of my meetings, which I’m happy to do.

“I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as mayor of Greater Manchester.

“None of it is recent, actually, in terms of the meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting, actually, and that was in 2021. That is right and I will put that all out there.

“But the football issues, they are serious and have to be dealt with, and the process is independent and it has to run its course. But I think everybody should separate the investment issues because they’re not the same thing.”



The Premier League said an independent commission found City arranged “sham” commercial deals with a number of its sponsors during the period, which were part of a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were required to pay only a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees.

The commission found that the remainder was funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan’s Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd, which majority-owned the club.

Shadow sports minister Louie French called for Mr Burnham to also “come clean” about any meetings since becoming Prime Minister and urged Sport Secretary Lisa Nandy to respond to questions.

“The Prime Minister must publish every contact between his ministers, officials and Manchester City since he walked into Number 10, the Prime Minister must also explain why he inappropriately intervened in this case, and Lisa Nandy must answer the questions I have put to her in full.”

It comes after Paul Parker, the England and Manchester United defender, blasted Mr Burnham for getting embroiled in the sporting row.



Speaking to PariuriX.com, Parker, 62, said: “It’s not a good picture for football. It’s an embarrassment to England.

“We want to tell everyone what we are – that we’ve got the best league in the world. Well, we’ve got the league with the most money.

“It’s going to be a long season. People aren’t going to be talking about whoever wins the league this season.

“Just win it and go away and enjoy it to yourselves. There’s no point in trying to make a big meal of it. No big PR drive.

“No-one will have any interest at all. No interest at all.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Can Man City win the league? Well, we have to ask: ‘Do the establishment need Man City to win the league?’

City’s UAE owners, who bought the club in 2008, have come under attack for the financial rule-breaking and brought into question where football sides should be State-owned.

Sports.title: Gary Neville cracks joke about Erling Haaland’s dad ‘distancing himself from Man City chiefs’ after he sits with FANS
Sports.content:

GARY NEVILLE cracked a joke about Alf-Inge Haaland after he was spotted sitting among the Manchester City fans at Anfield.

It was the first time Enzo Maresca’s players had taken to the pitch since the club was found GUILTY of more than 100 breaches of the Prem’s financial rules during a nine-season period.

City had been frustrated by the hosts until they were handed the advantage after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off in the second half.



Just three minutes later, Erling Haaland put the visitors ahead with a typically emphatic finish.

As the Norweigian striker celebrated, cameras picked up that his dad Alf was in the stands with the City supporters.



Alf is a regular attendee at games to show his support for his prolific son.

He said: “Maybe he’s distancing himself from the City executives.”

Sports.title: Konstantis Tzolakis suitors to hold talks with Hull NEXT MONTH as Liverpool target £40m Alisson transfer replacement
Sports.content:
Next

HULL are braced for transfer talks with suitors of star goalkeeper Konstantis Tzolakis NEXT MONTH amid his stunning start to life in the Premier League.

So impressive has he been there have been links with Liverpool.



Tzolakis, 23, became the Tigers’ most expensive keeper of all time this past summer after a £17million deal with Olympiacos, where he burst onto the scene in 2024 and won the Europa Conference League.

The Greece international went on to shine bright in the Champions League and Europa League with the Piraeus outfit against the likes of Arsenal, Real Madrid, Barcelona, Ajax and Bayer Leverkusen.



And that led to interest from Aston Villa, Coventry, Leeds, Brighton, Juventus, Atalanta, Roma, Napoli, Fiorentina, Leverkusen, Fenerbahce and Galatasaray until Hull won the bidding war.

Tzola then quickly became a key figure behind the Tigers’ flying start in their Prem return that saw them climbing up to eighth place, which could lead to European qualification this season.

The Crete native already counts a total of three clean sheets in all of his six appearances.

In fact, the Greek star became only the ninth keeper in Premier League history to pick up a clean sheet in all of his first three matches.

Tzola also stood out for his national team during the Nations League break as he caused Jurgen Klopp‘s first ever loss as Germany boss in Augsburg and kept a clean sheet in the return fixture that led to a goalless draw, while also shining against the Netherlands.

Reports in Spain suggest Liverpool are now keen to hold talks over a potential £40m deal for the shot-stopper.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

There have also been rumours recently suggesting Tottenham are keeping tabs as well.

However, SunSport understands no talks are expected to take place before mid-November.

Tzolakis is fully focused on Hull and the team’s goals, which include adding as much distance as possible between them and the relegation zone while also targeting an ambitious European qualification.

Liverpool icon Alisson’s contract runs out in June and thus manager Andoni Iraola may need to find a new No1.



It is currently uncertain whether Iraola would place back-up goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili as his first choice, and Tzolakis poses among the preferred options for that role.

Hull are highly unlikely to part with such an important figure before the end of the season but it also seems inevitable that big clubs are going to be knocking on their door after such fine displays.

Sports.title: Liverpool 0 Man City 3: Visitors survive fiery Anfield to win first game since verdict as controversial red changes game
Sports.content:
Next

BUSINESS as usual, Erling Haaland had promised.

And business as usual it was, as City ignored all the noise to make it six out of six in the Prem – and send Liverpool’s mocking taunts back into Merseyside throats.



An afternoon that was supposed to be about a national judgement on City for their financial misdemeanours ended in the way all of Enzo Maresca’s games at the helm have finished so far.

With City dominant and unstoppable.



Haaland’s eighth goal in seven City games this season, an instinctive, unstoppable finish as he reacted quicker than anyone in the Liverpool box, four minutes after Ryan Gravenberch was dismissed for a second yellow card, saw the Norwegian celebrate in front of his dad.

And when Jeremy Doku, who changed everything after his emergence from the bench, including inducing Gravenberch’s dismissal, bent into the top corner three minutes later, Liverpool, for all the Anfield passion play, were done and dusted.

That was confirmed when Rayan Cherki sent poor Jeremie Frimpong half way to the Birkenhead Tunnel before rolling in the third.

Say what you like about City – and EVERYONE has an opinion – you cannot fault their mental strength and quality.

Of course, it may end up counting for nothing.

The Liverpool fans who tried everything to make this a truly hostile environment will not be alone in hoping the ultimate punishment is one that changes everything.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Yet for now, as the travelling City fans revelled in home misery, it did not look as if Maresca and his men had even been aware of the carnage they might yet face.

In the end, the missing men in the Liverpool team-sheet, not only Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo but also Dominik Szoboszlai, did undermine Andoni Iraola and his side.

Yet first City had to walk through the storm, with Anfield engaged like rarely before, determined to be more than merely a 12th man, but a 13th or 14th.



Lewis Koumas, making his first Prem start and the scampering Victor Munoz discomforted Marc Guehi in particular, with the home supporters crackling with excitement at every tackle that flew in.

But for all the possession and territory, Liverpool rarely threatened, City looking far more composed when they did get on the ball.

With Florian Wirtz once again miles off it – will the German EVER look a £116m player? – Liverpool were unable to truly push or prosper. Iraola needs to see far, far more from Bradley Barcola, too.



By contrast, Elliot Anderson was a force of calm certainty, Cherki looking to weave his magic.

And a turgid first 45 minutes was forgotten by a manic opening to the second period.



First Koumas, then Ryan Gravenberch, were repelled by the diving Gigi Donnarumma, who was relieved when the third shot in less than a minute, from Alexis Mac Allister, whistled wide.

Chances coming, Milos Kerkez just beating Iliman Ndiaye to Antoine Semenyo’s driven cross with the goal begging.

When Haaland, who had barely been spotted, was played through by Semenyo on the hour, you expected the net to billow.

By his standards, it was a horrible miss, pulled wide with his right foot.



Yet seconds later, Gravenberch, booked earlier for a foul on Anderson, sent substitute Doku tumbling near the halfway line. The second yellow meant the long, lonely walk.

And by the time the Dutchman had taken off his socks, the 10 men were behind.

Doku cut inside Araujo, his shot deflected off Mac Allister and Haaland pounced, brilliantly and emphatically.



The Norwegian darted for the City fans, Matheus Nunes jumping on his back as dad Alf-Inge, in the midst of the travelling supporters, clenched his fists in acclaim.

Soon afterwards, Doku picked his spot from just outside the box, even Alisson helpless.

And after all 11 City players had touched the ball in a passage of play that left Liverpool playing statues, Cherki completed the destruction 12 minutes from time.



First he dummied Anderson’s pass, before running onto Josko Gvardiol’s sumptuous heel-flick, finishing it off by humiliating Frimpong to put the Dutchman on his backside before picking his spot.

No argument about this one, even if Anfield bellowed “cheats” at every City pass in the final seconds. It bounced off them. For now, at least, top of the pile.

Sports.title: How Antonelli could win F1 world title as soon as the next race
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli could become Formula 1's youngest world champion as early as the next race - the United States Grand Prix - on October 25.

Mercedes' Antonelli increased his lead at the top of the Drivers' Championship to a season-high 102 points with a third-place finish in the Singapore Grand Prix.

George Russell remains second in the standings but a ninth-place finish after engine penalties had left him starting at the back of the grid dropped him beyond a century of points behind his team-mate for the first time, while Lewis Hamilton's late slide off the podium leaves the Ferrari driver 111 points off the pace in third place.

With such a large lead and with a scheduled six races left in the 2026 season, the world title now looks a formality for the 20-year-old Italian in just his second year of F1 to usurp Sebastian Vettel as the sport's youngest title winner.

A first chance - albeit an outside one - to clinch the crown will arrive as soon as the next race at Austin's Circuit of the Americas, live on Sky Sports F1…

Image: How it stands after the Singapore Grand Prix

How Antonelli could win the title at the United States GP

There will be five scheduled races left - Mexico, Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi - after the United States Grand Prix takes place on Sunday October 25 and a maximum of 125 points left to play for.

To win the title in Austin, Antonelli needs to increase his championship lead by 23 points. For that to happen he must win the grand prix AND then hope both Russell and Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay within 124 points of him going to Mexico.

The permutations for Antonelli to become champion in Austin are:

Antonelli wins the race (25 points)

and

Russell finishes ninth or lower (2 points or less)

and

Hamilton finishes fifth or lower (10 points or less)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell takes over from Antonelli's engineer during the Sprint rain delay in Singapore

Were Antonelli to win the race and Russell finish ninth, Antonelli would hold a 125-point lead over his team-mate with exactly 125 points left to play for. But that would still be enough for Antonelli to become champion, provided Hamilton was also still outside the top four in the race.

That is because victory in Austin would be the the Italian's ninth of the year and with Russell on three wins the Briton would only be able to get to a maximum of eight in the five races left. Antonelli would therefore be guaranteed the title on results countback, with race wins the first tiebreaker in event of an end-of-season points tie.

What about the other drivers still in mathematical contention?

Max Verstappen (119 points back), Charles Leclerc (125 points back) and Lando Norris (139 points back) all remain in mathematical title contention too after Singapore but would all be automatically knocked out by an Antonelli win in Austin wherever they finished that race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff hits back at accusations that Mercedes favour Antonelli over Russell

'If I don't do my job well, then the result won't come' - Antonelli vows to stay focused

Antonelli is now within touching distance of an incredible historic achievement but stressed after Singapore that he cannot afford to let that fact distract him from his performance in Austin.

"I know it's very close, I know it's there, but I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can," he said.

"You know, the mindset is always the same, to go out there and win and perform the best way I can. I think this weekend [in Singapore] I haven't particularly driven that well. I felt like I could have done a better job, but I feel confident that, you know, a week to reset and I'm really looking forward to being back in Austin.

"But, at the end of the day, if I don't do my job well, then the result won't come. So in order to achieve what I want, I need to perform, as simple as that."

Sports.title: Man City defiant and top of the table - but Anfield delivers its own verdict
Sports.content:
The chant from The Kop went up early. "You haven't won a trophy since 1976." It was a reference to Manchester City's League Cup triumph, the last major honour that the club picked up prior to the period of ownership that now finds itself under such scrutiny.

As it is, City remain top of the table having won six games from six. But this victory will not quieten the noise. They departed to boos and the accusations of cheating that were a feature of the day.

Liverpool, three times runners-up to Manchester City in 2014, 2019 and 2022, made for perfect but hostile hosts, with the Anfield crowd perhaps the ideal outlet for the emotions, a proxy for supporters everywhere. It was an atmosphere like no other.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Man City arrive at Anfield ahead of their Premier League match against Liverpool - their first since being found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission

The enterprising flag and scarf sellers in Liverpool were certainly prepared, with an unusual emphasis on the visitors, this being City's first game since an independent commission judged that they broke Premier League rules between 2009 and 2018.

City are appealing that verdict and continue to deny any wrongdoing.

But the court of opinion is making its voice heard too. Anfield has made up its mind. The banners referred to "a generation of supporters cheated" and a playful take on Wonderwall with the amended line that "you really robbed us all".

Even the choice of songs over the public-address system appeared to be pointed. Before kick-off at Anfield, we had Blame by Calvin Harris and a blast of The Joker and the Thief by Wolfmother. Upon the final whistle, it was Little Lies by Fleetwood Mac.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roy Keane shares his thoughts on Manchester City following the club being found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City have lodged their appeal against the verdict

As expected, City's supporters opted for defiance in the face of the criticism. The boos for the Premier League anthem are nothing new but carried extra resonance. The banner declaring that 'In Khaldoon we trust' an eye-opening indication of the devotion of some.

Others preferred to shift the focus from their current predicament. There was more than a hint of nostalgia in a nod to the fact that there is far more to their club than how their rivals perceive them. Poznan dances and inflatable bananas served as a symbol of that.

The latter custom, one that dates back to Imre Varadi - 'Imre Banana' to the fans in the late '80s - is a reminder that City were always really here. This remains a proud club. The message being sent is that the downs are part of their story just as much as the ups.

Image: Man City fans wave inflatable bananas during their win over Liverpool at Anfield

But the overriding emotions inside the stadium belonged to the majority, those wearing Liverpool red, and the reality is that City and these charges are part of their story too. Anyone allowing the mind to wander at Anfield on Sunday could not escape that history.

Glance down to the spot on the turf where Steven Gerrard slipped to let in Demba Ba in 2014. Liverpool lost that game to Chelsea but lost that title to City. How can this ruling not change the tone and temperature of that regret? Sadness is now tinged with anger.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Micah Richards says he is devastated and confused by Manchester City's guilty ruling and claims that, as a player during the period in question, his integrity is being questioned

And so, for Liverpool, this is not only about City's trophies not being 'real' but those phantom triumphs of their own. "Until you've repaid the dreams you bought for your lies you'll be castaway alone under stormy skies." A banner in the Sir Kenny Dalglish Stand.

This game itself was a reminder that these matters are ongoing. The charges are historic but the consequences are part of the present.

A strange afternoon had a strange ending too - The Kop chanted 'going down' while the league table shows that City are top.

"That is the backdrop to not knowing where these points and this season is going," rued Gary Neville on commentary. "There is going to be a 'but' all the way."

Resolution cannot come soon enough.

Sports.title: 'Barely a foul' - Carra criticises 'shocking' Gravenberch red card decision
Sports.content:
Ryan Gravenberch's sending off in Liverpool's 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City was a "shocking decision" by referee Chris Kavanagh, according to Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.

Gravenberch, the standout player for an hour, was shown red after receiving a second yellow for a challenge on Jeremy Doku with the game tied at 0-0 in a flashpoint that turned the game, which had been finely poised, in City's favour.

Erling Haaland's opener came just two minutes and 37 seconds after Gravenberch was dismissed, and within six minutes Doku had doubled City's advantage before Rayan Cherki added a third with 12 minutes to play.

Gravenberch had picked up his first caution shortly after the restart for a foul on City midfielder Elliot Anderson, which Sky Sports pundit Carragher described as a "nothing challenge".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Liverpool’s match against Manchester City in the Premier League.

"It's such a poor decision by the referee," Carragher said after the game. "The thing that frustrates me is that he wasn't going to give a yellow card. He only gives it when he thinks Anderson is hurt.

"That has nothing to do with whether a foul should or should not be a yellow card."

He added: "It's barely a foul. It's a shocking decision."

"It feels really harsh when you think of the two challenges," Carragher said of Gravenberch's sending off on co-commentary.

"The first one was not a yellow card. It was so harsh for a nothing challenge on Anderson, and the referee was far too quick to get the yellow card out."

Sports.title: Man City issue on-field statement by beating 10-man Liverpool
Sports.content:
Manchester City shut out all the noise and controversy to overcome a hostile Anfield atmosphere and beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 on their return to Premier League action.

The trip to Merseyside was City's first game after an independent commission found them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules. The club have since appealed the verdict and continue to deny any wrongdoing.

The game's turning point occurred after an hour when Ryan Gravenberch was shown a second yellow card for a foul on Jeremy Doku - a decision called "very soft" on commentary by Gary Neville. Until then, City's xG was just 0.16. From then on, the floodgates opened.

Two minutes and 36 seconds after the sending off, Erling Haaland emphatically put City ahead before Doku and Rayan Cherki turned on the style as the Premier League leaders sent a message about what they are still capable of on the pitch.

The City players were welcomed by a chorus of boos for both their warm-up and ahead of kick-off as they settled into the Anfield cauldron.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Man City take to the pitch for the first time since being found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission. City have lodged their appeal against the verdict and deny wrongdoing

The game had mirrored the atmosphere in the early stages - frantic. The visitors were run ragged and on the receiving end of some strong tackles as the game threatened to boil over in the opening exchanges.

By half-time, City had managed to settle themselves and the crowd down. However, with Liverpool attacking The Kop in the second half, Enzo Maresca's men had to weather the storm all over again.

Gianluigi Donnarumma was on his toes to keep out multiple vicious strikes before Gravenberch's departure changed the game.

City's subsequent ruthlessness means they remain the only team to make a perfect start to the league campaign, with Andoni Iraola's Reds already nine points adrift following their first defeat.

'A moment to remember for a long time'

"You're thinking, 'Pep who?' at this stage. It's not even been mentioned the concerns we had when Pep left, or Rodri.

Sports.title: Miracle in London as Jaguars beat Eagles with field goal as time expires
Sports.content:
Cam Little kicked a 57-yard field goal as time expired to give the Jacksonville Jaguars a 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles in a miraculous ending at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw a 27-yard touchdown to Parker Washington on fourth down with under four minutes remaining to give them a 16-14 lead, and when they forced the Eagles to punt with two minutes left, the win looked all but secure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was a chaotic opening play between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguats at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as a 90-yard touchdown was called back due to flags and two players were ejected

But when Jalen Hurts led the Eagles 32 yards downfield in nine plays to set up a Jake Elliott 48-yard field goal with 12 seconds to go, the Eagles-heavy crowd celebrated what appeared to be a 17-16 Philadelphia win in London.

However, those 12 seconds were enough for Ameer Abdullah to stun the stadium with a 53-yard kick-off return, before Little hit the game-winner as time expired.

The Jags move to 4-1 on the season and look every part the Super Bowl contender after a supreme performance from Lawrence.

Image: Trevor Lawrence led the Jacksonville Jaguars to a comeback win

Meanwhile, after a turbulent season so far filled with injuries and disappointment, the Eagles fall to 2-3.

How it happened

The game started in as chaotic a fashion as it ended. Jacksonville's Josh Cameron took the kick-off back 90 yards for a touchdown, only for flags, hats and fists to fly. The play was nullified, players from both teams were ejected and the game restarted.

The Jags opened the scoring shortly afterwards. Lawrence rolled out to his right and hit Washington in stride, with the receiver racing down the sideline and cutting back for a 51-yard score.

Image: Parker Washington scored twice in a massive day

The Eagles struck back twice to take the lead, with Will Shipley's two-yard score followed by a 61-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper where, reminiscent of Washington's touchdown for the Jags, he beat defenders and raced to the end zone.

There was more drama before the half, as the Jags drove 68 yards in a 17-play drive, only to be stopped four times from the Eagles' one-yard line and leave the score at 14-7.

Image: The Eagles defense stopped the Jags at the goal line twice

Little added three points in the third quarter but both teams fully took hold of the game. Quinyon Mitchell intercepted Lawrence, while Hurts missed a wide-open Dontayvion Wicks as the Jags sent all-out pressure on a third down.

The Eagles stopped the Jags again at the goal line, as the Philadelphia-heavy crowd forced a turnover on downs after a pair of delay-of-game flags, but when Lawrence had another chance to put together a drive, he did not waste it.

He dropped the ball right into the arms of a diving Washington for an incredible score.

After that, the pair of exchanged field goals provided a fitting ending to one of the great NFL games in London.

Sports.title: 'Very scary!' - Antonelli relieved Verstappen is not in F1 title fight
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli says it would be "very scary" if Max Verstappen was a championship rival after the Red Bull driver won the last two Formula 1 races.

Verstappen scored maximum points across the Sprint weekend in Singapore to add to his victory earlier this month in Malaysia but, unlike last year, is too far back to make a championship charge.

In fact, Antonelli could wrap up the title at the next race in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1, if he outscores Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 23 points and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 14 points.

Antonelli had another damage limitation weekend in Singapore but still finished on the podium in third after a good strategy call by Mercedes to give him fresh soft tyres to overtake McLaren's Lando Norris and Hamilton late on in Sunday's race.

It was an unexpected result given the new upgrades, which Mercedes introduced in Malaysia, were not giving the major performance gain the team expected.

"It would be very scary!" Antonelli told Sky Sports F1 when asked if he is glad Verstappen is not in this year's championship battle.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen wins his first ever Singapore Grand Prix

"All in all I feel like we are doing a great job. At the end, you look at the season, and we have always been there.

"Obviously we have had a great car and now we are trying to understand this new package. I'm very proud of the team this weekend because we pushed through the difficulties and started to see life at the end of the tunnel. It's just a matter of time.

"Now we go to Austin, a normal weekend, where we can hopefully do a lot of changes and understand the package more."

Image: F1 Drivers' Championship ahead of United States Grand Prix

Antonelli, 20, is set to break Sebastian Vettel's record of being the youngest F1 world champion and has six races to get over the line.

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff is usually cautious with his expectations but even he admits Antonelli is almost certainly going to win the title.

"You look at the numbers and ask the probability of him winning, and it's probably almost 100 per cent. But it's motor racing, you can break down, you can have accidents, and then things could start to stress," he told Sky Sports F1.

"So, I think we need to look at it race by race, make sure that we are continuing to score the points, and eventually hopefully it's going to come towards him."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff hits back at accusations that Mercedes favour Kimi Antonelli over George Russell

Verstappen: Maybe Lambiase was happy radio was not working!

Red Bull's recent resurgence appears to have ended Mercedes' large dominance over the season, although Verstappen's win in Singapore was not straightforward as he was unable to talk to the team for the whole race.

Verstappen, who has won at every track on the calendar apart from Madrid, could hear his engineer Gianpiero Lambiase, but not the other way around.

"Maybe he was happy that it was not working! I couldn't really say anything. He did try at one point to ask me a few things in code, and I think he understood well what I meant or did not do," said Verstappen.

"But it's never nice. I've been having difficulty with my radio already the whole season, and this weekend has been particularly bad."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen reacts to winning the Singapore Grand Prix

The biggest threat to Verstappen's win came at the start from Charles Leclerc as Red Bull have been poor off the line throughout 2026.

However, Verstappen got a good enough launch to move to the inside and pinch Leclerc, forcing the Ferrari driver to brake early and back out of the move.

"The start was critical, so that was just good enough. Something was not particularly right at the start, so I need to understand what went wrong there," he said.

"Before releasing the clutch, it didn't feel good. But it was just good enough. Then we had a few laps with some deployment issues, so that's where Charles almost got me actually into Turn 7.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the start of the Singapore Grand Prix where Max Verstappen held off Charles Leclerc

"Once we had cleared the deployment problems, it was fine. The car was really good on the tyres. I could really manage them well.

"But to be honest, I think it was one of the first times that I've driven in clean air here in Singapore in the race, so I guess that's also nice.

"It's been just a fantastic weekend for us. I mean, we were flying on the soft, we were okay on the medium, and then of course with the VSC, I think it was right what Charles did with pitting and going back on a soft tyre. But, we just had it under control and of course, really happy to win here."

Sports.title: Cummins helps Australia take control against South Africa
Sports.content:
Pat Cummins claimed 3-54 as Australia took a 139-run lead against South Africa at stumps on day three of the first Test in Durban.

A collective bowling effort from Australia saw South Africa bowled out for 284 in their first innings, with Mitchell Starc (2-63), Josh Hazlewood (2-54) and Nathan Lyon (2-58) also among the wickets.

Australia scored 390 runs in their first innings with Matt Renshaw hitting a career-best 190 to help the visitors recover from a precarious 124-6.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Steve Smith took a trio of great catches as Australia gained control of the first Test against South Africa

In their second innings, Australia were 33-0 at stumps from 5.4 overs - Nic Maddinson 17no and Travis Head 10no - when play was called off early again due to bad light, with nearly 13 overs lost in the day.

David Bedingham top-scored for South Africa with 49 off 73 balls. The hosts were 197-8 at one stage before a 52-run ninth-wicket partnership between Keshav Maharaj (34) and Simon Harmer (35no) repaired some of the damage.

South Africa are the reigning world Test champions and beat Australia in the 2025 final. It is Australia's first trip to the country since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal when they last toured there.

Australia bowlers make difference on day three

Image: Australia captain Pat Cummins fields-off his own bowling

South Africa were down to 115-4 at lunch. Starting from 27-1 on day two, Aiden Markram (37) and Bedingham added 57 runs to their overnight partnership.

The breakthrough for Australia came just before drinks when Markram edged Starc to slip in the 21st over.

South Africa scored 59-1 in the first hour. In the second hour, Temba Bavuma (3) was out caught off Lyon - Steve Smith taking a well-judged catch as Bavuma went for a reverse sweep.

Image: Australia's Travis Head takes a catch and dismisses Marco Jansen

Cummins then had Bedingham caught in the slips with Smith taking another great catch to his left.

After lunch, Cummins struck again. Wiaan Mulder was the first to go - he scored 30 off 50 balls with three fours and a six, adding 56 with Tristan Stubbs.

Stubbs fell soon after for 32 - caught at square leg, again off Cummins.

Image: South Africa's Jansen plays a high ball

Lyon had Kyle Verreynne caught at slip for 13 as South Africa stumbled to 197-7. Marco Jansen hit six fours for a 20-ball 26, before holing out off Hazlewood.

South Africa were 238-8 at tea with Harmer and Maharaj able to go past the follow-on mark. Their 50-partnership ended when Starc dismissed Maharaj.

Sports.title: Smith vows 'karma' will get Suljovic after antics at Swiss Darts Trophy
Sports.content:
Ross Smith has vowed that "karma" will catch up with opponent Mensur Suljovic after the Austrian encouraged the crowd to boo the Englishman during a last-leg decider in round three of the Swiss Darts Trophy.

The two players were deadlocked at 5-5 in their best-of-11-legs clash on Sunday afternoon, with Smith having two match darts at double 18 when Suljovic gestured to the crowd to increase the volume of boos, prompting the Englishman to miss the target and give his opponent a chance at the match.

Suljovic then nailed a double 10 with his last dart to secure the checkout and the victory, although his unsportsmanlike antics left a sour taste in Smith's mouth, later taking to X to post his thoughts after the defeat.

"I don't blame Mensur for me losing that game," Smith wrote. "I missed two match darts. Simple as that.

"Obviously it's impossible for me to know what he's doing behind my back when I'm throwing apart from the crowd's response.

"If he wants to be an absolute helmet that's on him - karma will come around."

Image: Suljovic was involved in controversy during a match against Joe Cullen at the World Championship

Suljovic is no stranger to controversial incidents. The Austrian denied intentionally provoking Joe Cullen during a World Championship clash last December.

Cullen described his pace of play as like "cheating" and "not darts" after 'The Rockstar' was unhappy with the length of time his opponent was taking to recover his darts and the time he was taking to celebrate - with referee Kirk Bevans even forced to intervene.

"I never, ever do this as a provocation," Suljovic said in his response to Cullen. "I do it only for my game.

"I like my game - I never do it to be a villain. Sorry Joe, I never do this - I love you man."
