Sports.title: Max Verstappen was brilliant in cruising to Singapore victory... but it's just a matter of time before wonderkid Kimi Antonelli clinches his maiden title, writes JONATHAN McEVOY
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli, at 20, is the Formula One champion-elect and nobody can get near to him. It’s all over and the rest can switch their engines off right now.

Yes, Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix, his 73rd triumph but his first here under the lights of the city track. It was another demonstration of the Dutchman’s brilliance, a dominant win from pole that was never in doubt in a largely boring race.

Antonelli, the great aggregator from Bologna, finished third, separated from Verstappen by Charles Leclerc of Ferrari.

So strong has Antonelli been this season that he can secure the title in Austin, Texas, home of the next race, a week on Sunday. He will do it in the end, wherever he does it, having made practically never a slip even on his average days.

And George Russell, the British drive who carried every hope of accomplishing that dream in the other Mercedes, is gone. Game over. Long blown away. He is 102 points back, and that is nowhere you want to be when your lifetime’s work is on the line.

He finished ninth yesterday. He is resigned to his predicament, though he will not quite so readily admit to it. With six races remaining – if Formula One’s owners follow through on the idea of concluding the season in the Middle East.

Max Verstappen celebrates his second win in a row after a dominant drive

Verstappen successfully handed an early move from Charles Leclerc (right) to stay in front

If they switch to Imola to fill in for the potential absence of one or two rounds in that region of the world after bombs fell on Saudi Arabia yesterday, he remains condemned to disappointment. It’s relevant. This is in brackets, as it were, but he needs to move teams or forever serve as a player in another man’s script – as Antonelli’s Jeeves.

As for Verstappen’s tremendous victory, by 10 seconds over Leclerc, this must be saluted. It reflects the fact that his Red Bull team are on a march and, and that their engine, newly made under the auspices of Christian Horner, who set up the enterprise several years ago before leaving last season, is a huge success.

Lando Norris was fourth and Lewis Hamilton sixth, a place behind Oscar Piastri of McLaren.

Antonelli came up one place from where he started on the grid – he is streets ahead in the overall fight and on the day he did what he needed to do to secure his advantage in this regard. He needs to be 126 points in front after Austin, the next race, to clinch the championship. Nearly a job done at barely out of his teens.

Hamilton was in a war of words with Ferrari as he vied with Leclerc for his track position, deciding to stay out on old tyres, a policy that he later acknowledged did not work, and that he was the one in the wrong.

‘Sorry boys,’ he admitted. ‘I let you down today with that strategy. My call, and I lost us valuable points. I’ll try to make up for it in the next one. A painful lesson, but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made.

Kimi Antonelli, champion elect, added 15 points to his tally and can win the title at the next race

‘Not every call will work out and I can accept getting it wrong but I’m sorry for the team for the points we lost today. They put so much into every weekend and I wanted to deliver more for them. Great job with the pit stop though.’

Hamilton’s Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur said: ‘We asked him to pit. Don’t blame the team guys. Clearly on the radio he apologised and said, “It was my call”. He decided not to stop behind the virtual safety car but we would have been P2 and P3.

‘We were not sure we could go to the end so we chose to stop under VSC. There was a radio message. The driver has apologised that he let the team down.

‘It was very clear. We were P2, P3 on track, we called two of our guys to pit behind the VSC, one of our guys said, “no I prefer to stay on track” or he missed pit entry. Don’t blame the team.’

Lewis Hamilton admitted to a mistake in strategy that cost him a place on the podium

The triumphant Verstappen had no such concerns or recriminations. He said: ‘For sure I can dare to dream (of the title)… but at the same time, I know it is very close, I know it is there – but I need to make sure that I keep doing the best job I can, to go out there and win and perform the best I can.

‘This weekend I don’t feel like I have driven that well. I feel like I could have done a better job.

‘I am looking forward to being back in Austin but, at the end of the day, if I don’t do my job, the result won’t come.’

‘It is very difficult, so it is hard to say if I will be in the fight in Austin. I will just take it race by race and we will see how it goes there.

‘The car has felt a lot nicer from Baku onwards, a lot more balanced. The way that we have turned that around and the progress we have made makes it feel nicer.

‘When you can add podiums and wins too, that’s nice. We are not in the championship fight and that is why I think until the end we will try to have a good time and hopefully add more wins.’

There will be more for him before the end of the year, but the momentum is with Antonelli, drop by drop, increment by increment, and he will be winning the crown - possibly before the month is out.

Sports.title: Hull 2-2 Everton: Toffees' unbeaten start continues two days after owners revealed plan to sell and despite calamitous transfer window as Mohamed Belloumi salvages draw for the Tigers in exhilarating second half
Sports.content:
These are curious times at Everton, one of English football’s grand old institutions with owners that want out but whose unbeaten start to the season continued after a thrilling second half.

After a goalless opening 45 minutes, the game ignited in exhilarating fashion.

Boyhood Liverpool supporter Joe Gelhardt fired Hull ahead but Everton hit back to lead with goals from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry before home substitute Mohamed Belloumi kept his composure to rifle home a superb equaliser.

In the end, a draw felt about right after an absorbing encounter which capped a turbulent few days for Everton boss David Moyes, his players and supporters.

On Friday morning, and just 22 months after taking over from Farhad Moshiri, confirmation that the Friedkin Group (TFG) wish to sell the club arrived.

The news came as no real surprise after last term’s top scorer Beto and prized asset Iliman Ndiaye were both sold on deadline day.

Attempts to cash in on highly-rated teenager Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest were kiboshed after fans threatened to riot.

Nevertheless, it was a calamitous transfer window which left Moyes with just 18 outfield players and one striker.

Mohamed Belloumi earned a point for Hull with his well-struck shot making it 2-2

The Hull star celebrates passionately after scoring his third goal of the season

And yet despite everything, Everton are now unbeaten in six Premier League games, although they let slip a lead after coming from behind during the second half.

Gelhardt, a Scouser and boyhood Liverpool fan who spent time in the youth ranks at Everton before being released, opened the scoring with a neat finish in the 48th minute.

Gelhardt celebrated in style but the visitors levelled seven minutes later, though, with a close-range header from Dewsbury-Hall and Barry then blasted home a second with 22 minutes remaining.

Yet Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic has fashioned some spirit in his side and Belloumi fired home a superb 74th-minute equaliser to deny Everton victory.

An entertaining first half saw both sides fashion numerous half-chances and Everton’s Brennan Johnson have a goal ruled out for offside following a VAR check.

Hull fought and scrapped for every ball and midfielder Matt Crooks twice hacked down Jack Grealish cynically in the opening quarter, the second of those challenges earning him a booking.

It said much for the uncompromising approach of a newly-promoted Tigers outfit who themselves have begun the season in encouraging fashion.

Jakirovic’s men were never going to allow the likes of Grealish, James Garner and Dewsbury-Hall to pop the ball around with their usual swagger.

Thierno Barry finishes coolly to put Everton 2-1 ahead midway through the second half

And having survived some nervy moments in the first half, Hull led shortly after the break when Oli McBurnie expertly found Sorba Thomas, whose clever pass played in Gelhardt.

The former Wigan and Leeds man cleverly lifted the ball over the onrushing Jordan Pickford with a neat left-footed finish and the MKM Stadium erupted.

The response from Everton was impressive and emphatic as Dewsbury-Hall stooped to head home a deep cross from Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

After Thomas’ errant pass gifted Everton possession, Hull were made to pay as Dewsbury-Hall’s touch fell kindly to Barry to fire home right-footed.

Still, Hull were not finished and good work from Elliot Stroud on the left flank saw him find Belloumi, who controlled the ball and created the space to rifle a shot past Pickford from 12 yards.

Cue more Hull delirium and delight as the Tigers maintained their unbeaten home start and Everton headed back to Merseyside still to taste defeat this season.

Sports.title: Dominic Solanke led the line expertly and repaid Roberto De Zerbi for his show of faith - his rescue act needs to be the catalyst to kick-start Spurs' season, writes MATT BARLOW
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi has a lot hinging on Dominic Solanke. Perhaps not all of it by design but by ostracising Richarlison, selling Will Lankshear and signing Omar Marmoush who does not look like a natural fit at centre forward in this system, the Tottenham boss needs Solanke’s fire to rekindle.

Having spent the international break working on him and the three forwards in support, none of whom were away playing for their countries, the Spurs boss asked him to lead the team at Old Trafford in every sense.

Solanke was given the honour of pulling on the armband and being the captain despite not being part of the five-man captaincy group.

It was, according to De Zerbi, a popular move to show faith in a striker who has been the target for criticism during Spurs’ sluggish start to this season.

He started by missing a sitter and the time it took to collect the ball and work it into a shooting position portrayed his fragile confidence. Senne Lammens made a good save, but the Spurs skipper should have scored.

Dominic Solanke netted his first of the season to lift Spurs' spirits

Then he missed another glorious chance at the start of the second half but to his credit he kept going. He refused to let the misses haunt him. He held up the ball, fought to protect it when he could and drew Manchester United’s centre halves into a physical contest.

In the end, Solanke earned his reward, outmuscling Lisandro Martinez to reach the teasing, inswinging cross from Sandro Tonali, the midfield general signed for a club record £100million who finished the game at left back from where he delivered his most significant contribution in a Spurs shirt.

Tonali’s relief was clear. He is impatient to make an impression and produce a return on what he realises is a huge investment, and yet it will be nothing compared to Solanke’s.

Centre forwards need to score, and he was his first in the Premier League since March. His problems in front of goal since returning from an ankle injury which ruled him out of the first half of last season have been amplified by the team’s problems finding the net.

There was no way Solanke was going to let anyone think he had not applied the slightest touch to the ball. He raced away to a jubilant away end to bask in the glory.

Solanke's header was his first league goal since March

De Zerbi applauded his performance. 'We need this Dominic Solanke because Dominic Solanke is able to make the difference in this team,' said the Spurs boss.

Having been reduced to 10 men, his team showed some of the fighting spirit they have been accused of lacking in the last 12 months.

As a collective, Solanke’s equaliser cast a positive glow across another game when they have failed to win.

Three points from six games is barely cause for celebration but De Zerbi has been searching for what he called a ‘click’.

Perhaps this goal will be it. Something to change the narrative. Perhaps to instil faith in what they are trying to do.

Something also to remind them they can fight back. De Zerbi adored the reaction. 'The first time we have played as a team,' purred the Italian.

Spurs have not come back from behind to win in the Premier League for almost two years and the counter has ticked to 49 games.

It is an embarrassing statistic but fighting back to take a point with 10 men will go down as progress and De Zerbi will be thrilled at Solanke’s part in the rescue act.

Rodrigo's red mist

Spurs have often been guilty of emotional fragility in the last two seasons. Start well but fail to score, make a mistake, go behind and then crumble. It has been a familiar routine.

So when they started well at Old Trafford only to fade and go behind, then see Rodrigo Bentancur lose discipline and leave them a man down as well as a goal down it seemed like another one of those days.

Bentancur is one of De Zerbi’s favourites because he is canny and experienced, and a little bit cynical.

Rodrigo Bentancur saw red in the second-half and was sent off for headbutting Luke Shaw

He started on the bench after a long-haul international break playing friendlies for Uruguay in India, South Korea and Japan, and came on when the game was goalless.

Within seven minutes, Spurs were behind and within five more he had left his teammates in the lurch by losing his head. First, jumping recklessly into a tackle and then springing up to headbutt Luke Shaw.

'I gave him a kiss and said thanks,' said De Zerbi. 'It’s a mistake but the red card gave us the spark. For a long time, Tottenham played without this blood and this character. I want to see it in every game. You can’t win with only quality but with the right energy we are going to win many games.'

Senesi shines

Centre halves in modern football are invariably the players with the most time on the ball and the most touches and it helps if they have vision and a good range of passing.

As Marcos Senesi’s composure shone in the first half it was tempting to wonder if Micky van de Ven’s future at Spurs will be at left back, where he plays for the Netherlands.

Senesi and Jan Paul van Hecke seemed perfectly comfortable together and relished the late rearguard.

Sunshine break

Spurs will go to Spain for a training break before the next game at home to Coventry on Monday week.

Sports.title: Inside Man City's dressing room after guilty verdict: We reveal Enzo Maresca's inspiring words which left squad 'ready to go to war' - plus the two most 'vocal and calming' stars
Sports.content:
In scenes that felt symbolic of the last fortnight at the Etihad Stadium, a huge lorry contracted to work on the site’s ongoing £300million redevelopment was impaled by an electronic bollard at about three o’clock on Friday afternoon.

Just stuck there in the car park, gallons of liquid leaking out of the bottom. Mercifully, the skewer puncturing the vehicle marginally evaded the fuel tank.

Almost exactly 24 hours earlier across Ashton New Road at the training ground, Manchester City bosses had been plugging any problems or uncertainty among their players.

Chief executive Ferran Soriano spoke to them as a collective, as he had with the Treble class of 2023 inside the first-team auditorium when the Premier League charges initially dropped. But it was the blunt, forthright message imparted by Enzo Maresca that had the squad sitting up and listening.

Maresca is forging a reputation as a strong communicator, as seen during his media duties before heading to Anfield, and there was one takeaway from his short private address.

‘Forget the noise,’ he told them. ‘We’re here to win a league. Let’s go and win the league.’

Man City boss Enzo Maresca has urged his side to win the Premier League despite the cloud hanging over the club after they were found guilty of breaching the top flight's financial rules

City CEO Ferran Soriano spoke to the squad as a collective after they returned from the break

Maresca stalks a dressing room when he talks, repeats mantras over and over, louder and louder. City’s players are listening to him and following him and it is little wonder that one source talked about being ‘ready to go to war’ because that is exactly the tone their manager is taking, with a delivery to boot.

This is also where previous relationships with Erling Haaland and Ruben Dias come in handy, the pair of them at the club when Maresca was Pep Guardiola’s assistant.

Those two are said to have been the most vocal among the squad since the guilty verdict was released a week last Tuesday, calming influences as others rightly worried about the ramifications of such a one-sided result that has taken everybody at City aback.

There are staff who are struggling to put the pieces together of what has transpired, comparing the certainty with the independent commission’s findings and the certainty of their employers that they will prevail on appeal.

Debating the seismic judgment with the credibility they see in Soriano and the affection they have for chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. These are confusing times for those in the offices.

‘A perceived external threat can strengthen a sense of togetherness, creating a feeling that the team needs to prove people wrong,’ said Dr Nikita Rowley, sport psychologist at Coventry University.

‘It is a double-edged sword. If it creates defensiveness, resentment or a siege mentality, it could increase pressure and distract players. The key is whether that feeling translates into positive collective focus and cohesion, rather than a preoccupation with outside opinion.

‘Breaking things down into manageable, immediate goals helps bring attention back to the present. Strong leadership, consistent messaging and an environment where people feel supported can help maintain trust and stability.’

Maresca has confronted drama before, the ex-Juventus midfielder interviewed and subsequently cleared of betting on Serie A matches as part of the Calciopoli scandal when his former club were demoted to the second division. He can lean on that experience with his players, who are waiting to be led.

That even goes for the more senior heads, with Haaland taken off media duties while away with Norway the day after news broke of the guilty findings for fear he would become the club’s spokesman before an official judgment had been published.

Once the globetrotting striker sat down with Sky Sports in the days before boarding the bus for Merseyside – an interview that had been slated for weeks beforehand – there had been discussions between the broadcaster and City about what might be appropriate to ask and how that was framed.

Together with Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland has been a vocal and calming member of the squad

Similar took place with Norwegian powerhouse Viaplay and other television rights holders before a Friday press conference that surprisingly passed off without incident.

And there is an understandable feeling within the club that footballers – however decorated and however articulate they are – should not present the face of this.

In Maresca, like Guardiola before him, they possess somebody adept at navigating this situation. In a different way, with a smile and quick line rather than confrontation, but somebody they can rely on nevertheless.

Those similarities extend to how to manage the squad, with Haaland having spent a few days in Marbella playing golf after being given time away from international duty at the end of the Nations League window, with those not away with their countries – the suspended Phil Foden, Antoine Semenyo – given breaks to travel too.

Semenyo is labelled ‘David Beckham’ this season by Haaland after stunning assists and got married during his time off.

Still smiling after the bombshell news and City will need to take that attitude with them on Sunday if they are to thrive in an environment that many will not have experienced before.

Sports.title: Liverpool fans issue Man City with stern reminder as pointed chanted rings around Anfield
Sports.content:
Liverpool fans issue Man City with stern reminder as pointed chanted rings around Anfield

Liverpool were outclassed by Manchester City, who still have the threaten of a punishment looming, which led the Anfield crowd to remind them of the possibility of relegation

View 2 Images Liverpool fans made their disapproval of Man City's actions very clear

The Anfield crowd made sure to remind Manchester City of their possible fate as they chanted "going down, going down" in the latter stages of their win at Liverpool.

‌



‌



The Premier League leaders were playing for the first time since being found guilty of 114 financial breaches by an independent commission. The anger among the Liverpool fans was notable, but it didn't impact on the City players themselves.

‌



Three second-half goals helped them secure their sixth win on the bounce to begin the season, but their exploits come amid the threat of major punishments, the most severe being relegation and the stripping of titles.

‌



Liverpool were outclassed in front of their own fans, but as the visitors ran down the clock the home crowd were sure to make the City players know that they could yet be playing in the Championship next season.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

City continue to protest their innocence and have appealed the decision. Their period of wrongdoing covered from 2009 to 2018 - and during that time they pipped Liverpool to the Premier League title by two points in 2014.

‌



A host of leading figures within the game believe City's punishment needs to be long lasting with former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher suggesting they should face a multi-year punishment, which would end up with players leaving, rather than them being relegated and returning within a year.

Pep Guardiola once claimed he would manage City even if they were relegated and Enzo Maresca refused to be drawn on his future, especially whilst the appeal played out, but equally maintained the players were determined to do their talking on the pitch.

View 2 Images Man City could yet be relegated following their guilty verdict

Article continues below

He said: "We completely understand the seriousness of the situation. I'm not saying we don't understand that. We understand, the players understand, but it's our duty, our job to try to control the noise. The managers and the players are focused on winning games, not about something different.

On his own future the Italian added: "I don't know. We are predicting the future. I'm worried about tomorrow, two days, three days, I don't know what's happening in the future. The only thing I can say is that I think it's fair from my point of view, from all of us, that we respect the process. There is an appeal ongoing, we'll see what happens."

Sports.title: Liverpool vs Man City LIVE: Hostile Anfield SILENCED by dominant City after Gravenberch red
Sports.content:
Welcome to Mirror Football's live coverage of the Premier League game between Liverpool and Manchester City.

Man City were found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules during the international break as an independent commission found that they had used 'sham' sponsorship deals to inflate their revenue. The club strongly deny the charges and have appealed but that will count for little for their trip to Anfield.

Enzo Maresca's side make the trip to Merseyside and could scarcely face a more hostile atmosphere than from Liverpool, one of the clubs most directly impacted. They were able to handle the pressure as to come away 3-0 victors after Ryan Gravenberch's red card.

Stay here for live updates...

Sports.title: Man City reduce Anfield to a hush but Premier League uncertainty leaves plenty of questions
Sports.content:
Man City reduce Anfield to a hush but Premier League uncertainty leaves plenty of questions

Manchester City rocked up to the lion's den and left with all three points by hammering Liverpool, which makes their spot on top of the Premier League all the more awkward as a punishment could yet come

View 2 Images Man City produced the perfect performance at a hostile Anfield

There was never a chance Liverpool supporters wouldn't be looking back in anger. Turning Anfield into a cauldron of seething hatred for a few spiteful hours.

‌



‌



Enzo Maresca had ordered his Manchester City players to block out the noise. Which is much easier said than done at a football ground like this one. At the best of times, Anfield is intimidating. At the worst of times, it can leave visiting footballers crushed and exposed.

‌



It once happened to the great Lionel Messi during a Champions League semi final between Liverpool and Barcelona. And City were heading into the lion's den at a time of full blown crisis. Few places feel the injustice of what City have been found guilty of, more than the red half of Merseyside.

‌



In two of the seasons City won the title under Pep Guardiola, they did so by just a single point ahead of Liverpool. Liverpool supporters believe those titles now belong to them.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And reminders of City's cheating in terms of breaking Premier League spending rules, were right there for all those in light blue to see. For one game, they had become part of the Anfield scenery.

‌



One banner unfurled in the far corner of The Kop read: "A Generation of Supporters Cheated." While another one said: "After All You Really Robbed Us All".

Weeks of talks between various authorities had gone into planning how this game could take place without serious incident. The hatred runs deep between these two clubs. Something history has shown us all. But City overcame the first hurdle of getting into the ground without coming under attack, like they did back in 2018 ahead of a Champions League clash. But more challenges lay ahead.

This was an afternoon for cool heads in a white-hot atmosphere. It felt like Liverpool had the support of an entire football nation behind them. Not to mention the rest of the league. While every free kick City got from referee Chris Kavanagh, was met with howling derision. But as half time approached, Anfield had almost been reduced to a relative hush.

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool's frustration is obvious in light of Man City's guilty verdict - which will be shared by their rivals

Maresca's men had drawn the sting from the place. Eliot Anderson indulged in a running battle with Alexis Mac Allister, determined to show he wouldn't be intimidated. Marc Guehi was colossal in the City defence, while Enzo Fernandez appeared to lap up the hatred being thrown at him each time he took a corner.

Perhaps home supporters were starting to realise their victims couldn't be bullied? Like human sponges, City had absorbed whatever had been thrown at them. Noel Gallagher had made the short trip to Liverpool and stood in the away end. And what he witnessed was a masterclass in mental strength, from a team under the microscope like never before.

‌



A group of players who have needed to find new levels of defiance and thicker skins. And so it was left to Erling Haaland to help provide his side with the last laugh. Kick-starting what felt like an avalanche of goals, to leave Liverpool buried. Anfield fell into a stunned silence. It was now hosting a wake for its own team.

Much has changed for City and English football in the last fortnight or so. But then again some things haven't at all. City have finished the weekend where they started it. Top of the table looking down the rest. For the time being, at least.

Which, for the rest of their rivals, might just be one of the hardest things of all to stomach. Because no-one still knows what any of this is all going to mean.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville agree on Ryan Gravenberch Liverpool red card vs Man City
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville agree on Ryan Gravenberch Liverpool red card vs Man City

Ryan Gravenberch was controversially sent off in the Premier League clash between Manchester City and Liverpool

View 2 Images Ryan Gravenberch's red card was soft according to Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher (Image: (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images))

Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville were in agreement that it was harsh for Ryan Gravenberch to be sent off for two yellow card offences. During the second half of Liverpool's Premier League clash against Manchester City, he was penalised with two cautions for a late tackle on Elliot Anderson and pull-back on Jeremy Doku

‌



‌



However, Carragher and Neville were both not convinced that he should have been dismissed. The former said on Sky Sports: "It feels really harsh when you think of the two challenges. The first challenge was not a card and the referee was far too quick to get the card out."

‌



"The first was the same, the referee was so quick to get a yellow out. Neville then added: "That is very, very soft." Gravenberch was quite clearly upset as he trudged off the pitch with Andoni Iraola swiftly readying Trey Nyoni to come in and fill the midfield void.

‌



Before he could actually be introduced, though, Erling Haaland put City into the lead within three minutes of the red card. Doku then fired in a superb second for the visitors with the Belgian ultimately changing the game in his side's favour after replacing Iliman Ndiaye in the 56th minute.

Prior to Gravenberch's dismissal, he was one of many that forced Gianluigi Donnarumma into a strong save with Lewis Koumas and Alexis Mac Allister also going close.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



Two goals down and at a man disadvantage, the game looked to have been decided in just six minutes but City later made absolute sure of the points.

In a move where every City star touched the ball, which included a clever flick from Josko Gvardiol and Rayan Cherki sitting down Jeremie Frimpong prior, the latter swept in a third under Alisson.

On the goal, Carragher said: "Well we can talk about Manchester City, players that they've brought in, the money that they've spent, when they have spent money, whether its legal or not, they've bought good players. He [Cherki] is one of them.

‌



View 2 Images Rayan Cherki was praised for his Manchester City goal against Liverpool

"Absolute quality since he come into the squad, what a goal that is. The less said about Frimpong the better, he is all over the place, wow."

The victory maintains City's winning start to the season but any points from now are under a cloud following their guilty verdict for 114 financial charges, as pointed out by Neville.

Article continues below

He said: "That's the problem for the league this season, Manchester City are an outstanding team but if they don't overturn this guilty verdict, these points will be taken off them. This is the cloud that hangs over the entirety of the game."

City continue to protest their innocence and have appealed against the outcome reached by the independent panel.

Sports.title: Trainers' title blow for Aidan O'Brien as Jan Brueghel ruled out of Champions Day
Sports.content:
Trainers' title blow for Aidan O'Brien as Jan Brueghel ruled out of Champions Day

The favourite for the Long Distance Cup on Champions Day will not run – dealing a setback to the Irish genius in bis battle with Andrew Balding for the British trainers' championship

View Image Aidan O'Brien's Jan Brueghel misses Champions Day

Jan Brueghel will not lead Aidan O’Brien’s trainers' title push in the QIPCO Long Distance Cup at Ascot on Saturday after suffering a leg infection. And the Ballydoyle trainer revealed his quest for a hat-trick of championships in Britain - and a ninth overall - will not run to the end of the year but end at Doncaster on Saturday week.

‌



‌



Jan Brueghel, the 7-4 favourite, was the shortest Ballydoyle contender for the five Group 1 races on the British Champions Day card at the start of trading.

‌



But O’Brien, who also has Scandinavia – the five-time Group 1 winner has an “outside chance" of taking part – and Queenstown in the £500,000 two-mile test, revealed: “Jan Brueghel won’t run.

‌



“We were preparing him for it and he just had a setback, so he won’t be there. He got an infection in his joint - it got badly infected in two hours but hopefully he will be back for next year.”

O’Brien, who is locked in a battle with Andrew Balding for the 2026 trainers’ crown, is set to run Minnie Hauk and Amelia Earhart in Ascot’s Fillies & Mares Stakes, with Constitution River and Gstaad holding entries -– “we haven’t decided which way yet” – in the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes and Champion Stakes.

‌



But while the championship runs until 31 December, O’Brien will not be sending runners to Britain after he bids for a record-extending 13th success in the Group 1 William Hill Futurity Trophy at Doncaster in 12 days’ time.

“We do what we think is the right thing by the horses,” he added. “Our next two goes in England will be Ascot next weekend and then the following weekend.

"And then that’s us finished after that - that’s the way it usually is.”

Article continues below

O'Brien's title bid was boosted when he won Saturday's Dewhurst Stakes with Darkness Falls.

O'Brien is 4-6 favourite with Paddy Power to win the trainers' title with Balding at 11-10.

Sports.title: Roy Keane says ex-Man City stars should be DISGUSTED by club's 'dodgy dealings'
Sports.content:
Roy Keane says ex-Man City stars should be DISGUSTED by club's 'dodgy dealings'

Roy Keane has given a particularly forthright response to Manchester City’s charges ahead of their clash with Liverpool at Anfield and sent a strong message to players of the Premier League side

View 2 Images Roy Keane has issued his verdict on Man City's guilty verdict (Image: Sky Sports)

Roy Keane has suggested he would be ‘disgusted’ if he was a Manchester City player following their landmark verdict. City were found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges put towards them by an independent commission.

‌



‌



The club has already submitted an appeal and that will be heard during a separate hearing. And while Keane has absolved the club’s stars of any blame, he has said that they should feel particularly let down by City’s behaviour during the period that they were charged for.

‌





‌



Speaking ahead of City’s trip to Liverpool on Sunday afternoon, he said: “This is nothing against the players or supporters, this is an ownership issue. If you’re going after the big prizes, we’ve been fortunate to pick one or two up. You want to do it honestly.

“You want to look back at your career and think we did everything. You win some games, you lose some games.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“You can’t be looking back at what Man City have done and found guilty of, I know there’s an appeal. We’ve been sitting here and praising Man City and saying they’re amazing and bringing in amazing players. And Pep turning really good players into superstars.

“But the way they were doing it, that’s the issue, nothing on the players. If I was a player and there were stories about stuff we were doing at Manchester United, I’d be disgusted. I’d be disgusted if there were any dodgy dealings and anyone cooking the books

‌



"Some people think this is a bit strong, but I wouldn't feel like I've earned a league title if there was something dodgy going on in the background. Absolutely not.

View 2 Images Keane has suggested City's players should feel 'disgusted' (Image: Getty Images)

“We talk about lads going out and giving their all and picking up injuries but that is your job, that’s what you’re supposed to do when you’re giving it your all.

‌



"You just hope everyone is else is on the same page and being honest and everyone else is trying to do it the proper way.

“I hear a lot of ex-players saying that Man City players gave it their all, we know that. That’s not the issue. But they had unbelievable players on the bench to come on and make them stronger and get them over the line against teams like Liverpool who are pushing each other.

“That’s what top-level football is about, we had it with Arsenal. You hope there is honesty. That's where respect comes into the game

Article continues below

“We’re footballing people. It’s difficult for us to talk about legal stuff, we play the game because we love it and are passionate about it but you’ve got to also have a bit of honesty.”

Sports.title: Ray Parlour accuses Arsenal star of 'not doing his job' in Leeds victory
Sports.content:
Ray Parlour accuses Arsenal star of 'not doing his job' in Leeds victory

Arsenal managed to get back to winning ways on Saturday as they came from behind to beat Leeds United at the Emirates Stadium but one star in particular has come in for criticism

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal came from behind to beat Leeds on Saturday (Image: Getty Images)

Ray Parlour has criticised Arsenal star Noni Madueke for his defensive efforts in the Gunners’ win against Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s side got back to winning ways on Sunday after coming from behind.

‌



‌



James Justin had given the Yorkshire side the lead but goals from Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes flipped the game on its head.

‌



In assessing the result, Parlour did have one complaint and that was Madueke’s efforts in attempting to stop Justin’s opener.

‌



Speaking to Premier League Productions, the former midfielder said: “I thought Leeds were the better team up to that 60th minute when they made the substitution, until the equaliser, and they deserved it.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“You could see the fans really enjoying the goal and it was an excellent goal, it really was. You’ve got to really concentrate on just getting your connection right with the pace and Justin certainly got that right."

He added: “Madueke has got to do better there. I played in the wide areas at times and you’ve got to track your runners as well.

“As much as you like going forward, you’ve got to do a good job for your team. He’ll be disappointed with what he sees there when he looks back at it.”

‌



View 2 Images Madueke has endured a tricky season so far with Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Despite that, Parlour did praise Madueke for his reaction as the England winger played a key role in Arsenal’s equaliser. He said: “He [Madueke] is better going forward, we know that.

“This is a very, very important goal, they were just about to make the substitutions as well. It was a real deep cross at the back post and it is a brilliant header across. Calafiori gets into a dangerous area and he finishes it.

‌



“It’s a little bit harsh if I say James Trafford maybe should have done better. It was a much-needed goal for Arsenal at that time because Leeds looked pretty comfortable before that goal.”

Madueke has endured a tricky season for Arsenal so far this term. The 24-year-old has made just three starts, one of those coming in the Premier League. His only goal of the season came in Arsenal’s Carabao Cup victory against Ipswich Town.

Madueke has been linked with a move away from North London in the January transfer window, with both Atletico Madrid and Juventus having emerged as potential suitors for the former Chelsea forward.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
