Sports.title: Agit Kabayel’s Tyson Fury Pick Leans on Old Memories
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel picks Tyson Fury to handle Anthony Joshua, but that pick relies on memories from a decade ago. Kabayel shared rounds with Fury back in 2016, sharing the ring with a fleet-footed heavyweight vastly different from the man competing today.

Kabayel credits Fury with superior ring IQ, even while respecting Joshua’s single-shot knockout power. His prediction leans on Fury having multiple paths to victory, yet those ancient gym sessions tell us very little about present-day form.

“The better boxer, the better boxing IQ [is with] Fury,” Kabayel told The Ring. “But only one guy in the heavyweight division can beat the guys with one hand. This is Anthony Joshua.” “I think Fury will win the fight. Points, KO, but we will see. My prediction is with Fury.”

The glaring flaw in Kabayel’s logic involves Fury’s faded mobility. The 2016 incarnation feinted opponents out of position, changed angles effortlessly, and slipped outside hitting range with ease. Combine that fluidity with his massive frame, and he became a nightmare to track down.

Recent outings show a far more stationary operator. Fury still knows how to manipulate range with his reach, yet recognizing open space is quite different from possessing the foot speed to claim it. Against someone carrying Joshua’s power, lingering in the pocket too long invites disaster.

Kabayel admits his sparring comparison carries an asterisk.

“For me, the hardest sparring was with Fury,” Kabayel explained, pointing out that he had logged three extra years of professional seasoning before testing Joshua in 2019.

That timeline skews the perspective. Kabayel met Fury as a raw prospect, then shared rounds with Joshua as a fully developed contender capable of holding his own.

Fury’s ring craft gives him a legitimate shot. Still, wondering whether his aging reflexes can execute his intentions remains the central issue. Kabayel’s glowing scouting report honors a long-gone fighter Joshua never has to face.

Looking at Fury across his recent outings, the double defeat to Oleksandr Usyk followed by soft recovery touches against plodding veterans like Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach, you are watching a fighter surviving on reputation and size rather than elite capability.

Beating Wladimir Klitschko in Düsseldorf was a psychological masterclass against an aging champion afraid to pull the trigger, and the 2020 demolition of Deontay Wilder was the absolute ceiling of Fury’s offensive bullying. Everything since has been a steady march into decline.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Expects Early Finish In Daniel Dubois Rematch
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley expects his rematch with Daniel Dubois to finish early, with either heavyweight capable of ending the fight before it reaches the later rounds. Their first meeting lasted 11 rounds, so Wardley’s prediction points to a quicker, more explosive second fight.

“It’s only going one way. It’s finishing early one way or another. It’s going to be a crazy night. Everyone, tune in,” said Wardley to Queensberry.

That “one way or another” qualification leaves room for both outcomes. Wardley knows the danger Dubois brings, even after beating him the first time. He is promising action without pretending that trading heavy punches comes without a cost.

Wardley’s overhand right gives him a clear weapon to take into the rematch. He has already described how he used it to counter Dubois’ jab in their first fight, making Dubois think about what could come back whenever he extended his left hand.

Dubois needs an answer to that punch. His jab can help him control the fight, but throwing it repeatedly without adjusting his defense could give Wardley the opening he is looking for. Wardley doesn’t need to change much if the same counter remains available.

Still, their first fight showed that hurting Dubois early and finishing him early are two different things. Wardley had success well before the stoppage, yet needed 11 rounds to complete the job. Chasing a quicker ending could also make him easier to hit if he becomes too eager after landing.

Wardley expects his supporters to add to the atmosphere on Saturday.

“It’s huge for me. Hometown boy, home grown. Had the club, the supporters, everyone behind me from the beginning,” he said. “So it does mean the absolute most and they’re going to make themselves heard on Saturday night.”

The crowd will be ready for the fireworks Wardley promises. Whether the finish comes early depends on how well Dubois adjusts, and whether Wardley can turn his next opening into something decisive.

Sports.title: Ricardo Sandoval Must Settle The Score With Mendoza
Sports.content:
Ricardo Sandoval must decide on his next fight after losing his WBA and WBC flyweight titles to Sergio “Yoreme” Mendoza last Saturday night in Chicago. The immediate rematch route is his only real play if Golden Boy has a return clause baked into the contract.

Mendoza was brought in as a late replacement, so Sandoval’s team likely secured rematch language. If they did, Sandoval has to trigger it immediately. He gave up all the leverage he built by beating Kenshiro Teraji in Tokyo, and nobody at 112 or 115 is going to offer him big money without those belts.

If there is no rematch clause, Sandoval is in no-man’s-land. The flyweight division moves fast. Unification bouts, big cards in Japan, and potential moves up to junior bantamweight are off the table for him. Those paydays belong to Mendoza now.

To rebuild, Sandoval has to face reality about his defense. Getting dropped three times inside five rounds by a guy coming off a second-round knockout loss shows Sandoval’s habits caught up to him. He relies on taking shots to give shots, but without elite sharpness, his punch resistance completely disappeared last night under Mendoza’s firepower.

Apart from a rematch, he needs a tune-up to see if his chin and punch resistance can hold up before trying to climb back into the top five of the sanctioning bodies. Sandoval should aim for spring 2027, ideally March or April.

That gives him roughly five to six months. He cannot afford another extended layoff, yet he took serious physical damage on Saturday night. Absorbing three knockdowns before getting stopped in the fifth round means mandatory medical suspensions and mandatory rest. He must keep his gloves off for at least sixty to ninety days to let his body recover. Rushing into hard sparring in November or December would be reckless.

Sitting out another year would kill what is left of his career, though. Inactivity was a major reason his timing, reflexes, and punch resistance betrayed him against Mendoza. At 112 pounds, fighters burn out quickly, and the division forgets former champions fast.

Flyweight is the wrong division to play the brooding, inactive contender. It is arguably the most unforgiving weight class in the sport because success relies almost entirely on twitch reflexes, hand speed, and conditioning. Those are the exact attributes that disappear when a fighter sits on the shelf.

Sports.title: Oscar De La Hoya Hesitates Over Schofield vs. Zepeda Unification
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya agreed to a Floyd Schofield–William Zepeda unification after being pressed during DAZN’s post-fight interview, but his initial response suggested little enthusiasm for matching his two lightweight champions.

Schofield had just captured the vacant WBA title by defeating Lucas Bahdi when De La Hoya announced his interest in unifying. That invitation became less straightforward once Chris Mannix brought up Zepeda, Golden Boy’s WBC champion.

“We want to unify the titles against anybody,” said De La Hoya to DAZN.

Mannix asked whether Zepeda would be next. De La Hoya’s answer sent the conversation toward Abdullah Mason instead.

“Well, maybe it’s not the fight to do next, but let’s go with Mason or any world champion in the WBC. Whoever it is, ‘Kid Austin’ is ready,” said De La Hoya.

Mannix returned to the obvious option: “Zepeda has got that WBC world title. Let’s take that fight next.”

“We’ll make that fight happen then,” De La Hoya replied.

That was an agreement, although it came after De La Hoya had already suggested taking another route. There was no date announced or indication that either fighter had accepted the matchup.

The hesitation is understandable from a business perspective. Golden Boy now has two lightweight champions it can promote separately. Each can headline title fights, build his audience, and pursue opponents from other promotional companies. Putting them together guarantees that one leaves without his belt.

Mason is with Top Rank, making him a different proposition. Schofield could lose that fight too, but a victory would bring another title into Golden Boy while preserving Zepeda’s separate championship run. An in-house unification offers no such possibility.

That does not establish De La Hoya’s motive, but it explains why “anybody” might become less appealing when the opponent is another revenue stream within his own company.

For Schofield, Zepeda would also be a tough first defense. His sustained pressure and punch volume would test the new champion’s ability to keep control while being pushed backward.

Zepeda also has an obstacle to facing Schofield next. According to EverythingBoxing’s Darshan Desai, the WBC has ordered him to defend against interim champion Jadier Herrera, with purse bids scheduled for October 20. Mason’s WBO mandatory is also due, with Joe Cordina ranked No. 1.

De La Hoya’s unification plans could therefore require approval from the sanctioning bodies or agreements involving the mandatory challengers before either fight can proceed.

Sports.title: Schofield Wins WBA Title As Sergio Mendoza Upsets Sandoval
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield claimed the vacant WBA lightweight title, while Sergio Mendoza delivered the night’s biggest upset by stopping unified flyweight champion Ricardo Sandoval on Saturday at Wintrust Arena in Chicago.

The Golden Boy Promotions and Most Valuable Promotions card aired on DAZN. Schofield’s title victory came with disputed knockdown calls, while Mendoza overturned expectations in the co-feature.

Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs), of Austin, Texas, defeated Lucas “Prince” Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs), of Niagara Falls, Ontario, by unanimous decision over 12 rounds. The judges scored the fight 116-110, 119-108, and 115-111.

Schofield’s speed and movement helped him win rounds, but Bahdi’s power made the contest more competitive than the widest score suggested. In the third, Schofield knocked Bahdi into the ropes, prompting referee Ben Rodriguez to rule a knockdown.

Bahdi hurt Schofield during a fierce sixth round and landed a right hand in the ninth that sent Schofield’s knee to the canvas without a knockdown being called. Rodriguez credited Bahdi with a knockdown in the eleventh, although Bahdi appeared to step on Schofield’s foot as he went down. Schofield stayed mobile in the final round to secure the belt.

In the co-feature, southpaw Sergio “Yoreme” Mendoza (28-1, 24 KOs), of Hermosillo, Mexico, stopped Ricardo “El Niño” Sandoval (27-3, 18 KOs), of Rialto, California, at 0:24 of the fifth round to capture the WBA and WBC flyweight titles.

Mendoza dropped Sandoval twice during the final half-minute of the second round, with referee Mark Nelson administering a count each time. Sandoval rallied in the fourth, outscoring the challenger, but Mendoza dropped him again early in the fifth. After Sandoval rose, Mendoza drove him into the ropes with another attack, prompting Nelson to stop the fight.

The defeat ended Sandoval’s reign in his first defense and disrupted his plans for bigger fights following a lengthy layoff.

Super featherweight Jan Paul Rivera (17-0, 7 KOs), of Salinas, Puerto Rico, defeated Abraham Perfecto (14-3, 9 KOs), of Tecate, Mexico, by unanimous decision over ten rounds.

Rivera dropped Perfecto with a left hook in the second, prompting a count from referee Tommy Gonzalez. Rivera lost a point for a low blow in the ninth but remained comfortably ahead, winning 99-89 on all three cards.

Cruiserweight Tristan “Sweet T” Kalkreuth (18-1, 13 KOs), of North Las Vegas, Nevada, stopped Ivan Rosado (12-1, 9 KOs), of San Juan, Puerto Rico, at 0:44 of the third round of their scheduled ten-round bout.

Kalkreuth dropped Rosado with a right hand to the chin in the first. A third-round flurry brought the intervention of referee Ben Rodriguez, with Rosado still on his feet.

Light middleweight Grant Flores (14-0, 10 KOs), of Coachella, California, stopped Mikey Dahlman (19-3, 17 KOs) at 1:48 of the second round.

Flores dropped Dahlman with a left to the body in round two. Dahlman beat referee Dave Smith’s count, but Flores followed with unanswered punches until Smith halted the contest.

Lightweight Jahmal Harvey (5-0, 4 KOs), a 2024 U.S. Olympian from Oxon Hill, Maryland, stopped Pedro Castaneda (9-2-1, 5 KOs), of Ciudad Juarez, Mexico, at 0:28 of the third round of their scheduled eight-round fight.

Boxing from a southpaw stance, Harvey landed a left hand to the chin that dropped Castaneda. Castaneda got up but was in no condition to continue, prompting referee Dave Smith to wave it off.

Super featherweight Cris Williams (15-0, 8 KOs), of Chicago, defeated southpaw Asa “Ace” Stevens (7-1-1, 2 KOs), of Waianae, Hawaii, by unanimous decision over eight rounds.

Williams controlled the opening four rounds and hurt Stevens in the seventh. The judges scored it 78-74 twice and 77-75, with Mark Nelson refereeing.

Minimumweight Naomy “Wonder Woman” Valle (16-1, 9 KOs), of San Jose, Costa Rica, defeated Sheyla Moreno by unanimous decision over eight two-minute rounds.

Valle’s cleaner punching helped her build a lead, and a point deduction for holding in the eighth did not prevent her from winning her professional U.S. debut. Dave Smith refereed the bout.

Heavyweight Joshua “The Rocket” Edwards (8-0, 7 KOs), a 2024 U.S. Olympian from Houston, stopped Craig Lewis (15-10-1, 8 KOs), of Detroit, one second into the third round of their scheduled eight-round contest.

Edwards controlled the first two rounds and hurt Lewis near the end of the second. Lewis could not continue because of an injury, and referee Tommy Gonzalez halted the fight at the start of the third.

Michael Vale served as ring announcer.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Beats Lucas Bahdi To Claim WBA Title
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield won the vacant WBA lightweight title Saturday night, using his speed and movement to beat Lucas Bahdi by unanimous decision in a fight that tested his ability to recover under pressure.

The judges scored it 116-110, 119-108, and 115-111 at Wintrust Arena in Chicago. Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs) earned the belt, but Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs) made him work considerably harder than the widest card suggested.

Schofield established his jab early, darting into range with combinations before moving away. Bahdi answered with heavier punches and body work, showing that he could trouble the quicker fighter when he found openings.

A left hook sent Bahdi into the ropes in round three, earning Schofield a knockdown and an early advantage. Bahdi absorbed the setback and continued looking for opportunities to land his power shots.

The sixth became a fierce round in which both fighters were hurt. Bahdi badly rocked Schofield with heavy punches, but Schofield fired back rather than allowing the Canadian to take complete control. His willingness to trade made the fight entertaining, although it also gave Bahdi the kind of contest he needed.

Schofield returned to movement and counters in the following rounds. That approach forced Bahdi to chase, and his difficulty cutting off the ring allowed Schofield to collect points without remaining in punching range.

The refereeing became a talking point in the ninth when a Bahdi right hand sent Schofield’s knee to the canvas without a knockdown being called. Bahdi received credit for a knockdown in round eleven, though their feet tangled during that incident.

Schofield stayed mobile in the twelfth and reached the final bell. He showed enough boxing ability to win, along with the toughness to recover when Bahdi hurt him. The next step is tightening his defense: his speed won rounds, but trading unnecessarily repeatedly exposed him to Bahdi’s biggest weapon.

Sports.title: Sergio Mendoza Shatters Ricardo Sandoval’s Plans With Upset
Sports.content:
Sergio Mendoza Cordova wrecked Ricardo Sandoval’s plans with a fifth-round stoppage, taking the unified WBA and WBC flyweight titles in a fight the defending champion was expected to win Saturday night in Chicago.

Mendoza (28-1, 24 KOs) dropped Sandoval (27-3, 18 KOs) three times at Wintrust Arena, recovering from a second-round knockdown of his own to deliver the biggest victory of his career. The referee intervened in the fifth as Sandoval could no longer cope with the challenger’s attack.

Sandoval had entered his first defense looking to build on the split-decision victory over Kenshiro Teraji that earned him both belts in Japan in July 2025. Instead, his return after more than a year of inactivity ended with those titles heading to Mendoza.

This was supposed to be the night Sandoval got moving again. A successful defense would have allowed him to pursue bigger fights from the position of a unified champion. Now, he faces the task of rebuilding after a damaging defeat, with those opportunities belonging to somebody else.

Sandoval briefly appeared to have the fight moving his way when a right hook put Mendoza down in round two. That success did not discourage the Mexican southpaw, who recovered and used his pressure and punching power to turn the contest.

Mendoza’s three knockdowns made this more than a champion getting caught once. Sandoval could not regain control as the challenger kept hurting him, and the fifth-round intervention ended his hopes of rescuing the defense.

The result was especially unexpected given Mendoza’s recent form. He entered after a second-round knockout loss to Thanongsak Simsri in April, making his U.S. debut as a late replacement and heavy underdog.

Sandoval’s long absence invites questions about his sharpness, but Mendoza supplied the decisive punches. An opponent expected to help launch the champion’s next run instead took both belts and forced Sandoval to start over.

Sandoval walked into Chicago treating Mendoza like a stay-busy fight to dust off fifteen months of rust, and he paid the ultimate price for it. When a unified titleholder sits out for well over a year, thinks he can just show up against a heavy puncher, and gets dragged into a firefight, this is exactly what happens.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield vs Lucas Bahdi Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Lightweight Floyd Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs) defeated Lucas Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs) by unanimous decision to win the vacant WBA title, with scores of 116-110, 119-108, and 115-111. Schofield used his speed, jab, and lateral movement to win rounds, earning a knockdown in the third when a left hook sent Bahdi into the ropes.

Bahdi’s power kept the fight dangerous, badly rocking Schofield during a fierce sixth round in which both men were hurt. A right hand sent Schofield’s knee to the canvas in the ninth without a knockdown being called, while Bahdi received credit for an eleventh-round knockdown despite their feet tangling.

Schofield stayed mobile in the final round and reached the bell to secure the decision after a competitive fight marked by disputed refereeing calls.

Flyweight Sergio Mendoza Cordova (28-1, 24 KOs) upset Ricardo Sandoval (27-3, 18 KOs) by fifth-round stoppage to capture the unified WBA and WBC titles. Mendoza dropped the defending champion three times, turning his late replacement opportunity into the biggest victory of his career.

Sandoval scored a knockdown with a right hook in round two, but Mendoza recovered and took control with his pressure and power. The southpaw’s attack eventually forced the referee to intervene in the fifth, ending Sandoval’s first title defense.

Mendoza entered as a heavy underdog after suffering a second-round knockout loss to Thanongsak Simsri in April. Sandoval’s return after more than a year out ended with him losing both belts to a challenger making his U.S. debut.

Lightweight Jahmal Harvey (5-0, 4 KOs) stopped Pedro Castaneda Castro (9-2-1, 5 KOs) in the third round of their scheduled eight-round bout. Harvey controlled the action with his speed and accuracy before ending the fight with a sharp lead left cross.

The punch dropped Castaneda heavily and brought the referee in for a count. Castaneda managed to get back to his feet, but his condition prompted the referee to wave it off. Harvey needed no follow-up attack, with the single shot doing enough damage to force the stoppage.

The 2024 U.S. Olympian showed the value of a clean, well-timed punch against an opponent who could not match his skill. It was another early finish for Harvey, whose speed made the decisive left hand difficult for Castaneda to anticipate.

Super featherweight Jan Paul Rivera-Pizarro (17-0, 7 KOs) defeated Abraham Perfecto Valdez (14-3, 9 KOs) by unanimous decision over ten rounds. All three judges scored the fight 99-89 for Rivera-Pizarro.

The Puerto Rican scored a knockdown in the second round, establishing an early lead that Valdez never threatened. Rivera-Pizarro controlled the action with cleaner punching and a steady work rate, preventing the taller Mexican from building momentum. Valdez struggled to establish his offense and spent much of the contest being outworked.

Despite the early knockdown, Valdez lasted the distance as Rivera-Pizarro continued collecting rounds through the final bell. It was a comfortable victory for Rivera-Pizarro against an opponent coming off a fourth-round stoppage loss to Leonardo Sanchez.

Tristan Kalkreuth (18-1, 13 KOs) stopped previously unbeaten Ivan Rosado (12-1, 9 KOs) at 0:44 of the third round in cruiserweight action. Kalkreuth used his height and reach to control the scheduled ten-round fight, leaving the shorter Rosado struggling to get his offense going.

The 24-year-old pressed the action and overwhelmed Rosado with his power. Rosado could not adequately defend himself as Kalkreuth continued the attack early in round three. The referee stepped in with Rosado still on his feet, ending a one-sided contest. Rosado’s unbeaten record offered little protection against the larger Kalkreuth, who dictated the fight throughout.

Heavyweight Joshua Edwards (8-0, 7 KOs) stopped Craig Lewis (15-10-1, 8 KOs) at the start of the third round of their scheduled eight-round bout. The 2024 U.S. Olympian controlled the action against the 42-year-old veteran, forcing him onto the defensive.

Edwards landed a combination late in the second round that hurt Lewis and brought the fight toward its finish. Lewis could not continue because of an injury, prompting the stoppage at the beginning of round three. The injury’s exact nature was not specified in the early ringside account. Edwards needed just two completed rounds to register his seventh stoppage victory.

Grant Flores (14-0, 10 KOs) stopped Mikey Dahlman (19-3, 17 KOs) in the second round of their scheduled eight-round light middleweight bout. Flores controlled the action with his size and punching power, putting the veteran under pressure early.

A hard left hook to the liver hurt Dahlman badly in round two and opened the door for the finish. Flores followed with a sustained attack as Dahlman struggled to recover from the body shot. With Dahlman unable to halt the assault, the referee stepped in to stop the fight. The 21-year-old Flores needed fewer than two rounds to secure his tenth knockout.

Minimumweight Naomy Valle (16-1, 9 KOs) defeated Sheyla Moreno Castillo (5-2-1) by unanimous decision over eight rounds in her professional U.S. debut. The judges scored it 78-73, 78-72, and 77-74 for Valle. Valle controlled most of the early action with her jab and right hand, landing the cleaner punches as Moreno pressed forward.

A right hand in the third round hurt Moreno, but the Mexican fighter kept coming and made Valle work throughout. The final two rounds became scrappier, with Valle losing a point in the eighth for excessive holding after repeated warnings. The deduction came too late to threaten Valle’s lead, which she had built through her more accurate punching over the first six rounds.

Ghana News.title: ECG announces power outage in parts of Tema, Central Region due to network fault, maintenance
Ghana News.content:
The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced a power outage affecting parts of the Tema Region due to a fault in its network, while several communities in the Central Region will experience a temporary interruption in electricity supply on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, to allow for planned maintenance works.

In a notice to customers, ECG’s Tema Region said the network fault had affected Comm. 17, Timber Market, Resolve Hospital, Bakeshop, Marina Mall at Spintex, Baatsonaa and surrounding areas.

The company said its engineers were working to resolve the fault and restore electricity supply to the affected communities.

ECG apologised to customers for the inconvenience caused by the unplanned outage and assured them that efforts were underway to address the problem.

The company did not specify when power supply would be fully restored to the affected areas.

Meanwhile, ECG has scheduled planned maintenance works for Tuesday, October 13, from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., which will result in a temporary power outage in several communities, mainly in the Central Region.

The affected areas include Komenda, Kissi, Ayensudo, Ampenyi, Elmina, Eguafo, Aburansa, Besease, Ebu Krom, Agona Town, Breman, Iture, Duakro, Amamuma, and surrounding communities, as well as several other towns and settlements listed in the company’s notice.

The company said the maintenance exercise forms part of efforts to improve service delivery and apologised in advance for the inconvenience customers may experience.

ECG has urged affected customers to take note of the scheduled outage and make the necessary preparations ahead of the exercise.

Ghana News.title: When the Gospel Becomes a Weapon: The church, blackmail and the abuse of faith
Ghana News.content:
Let me begin with a clear declaration. I am a Christian. I believe in Jesus Christ, the Son of God and my Redeemer. I believe in the preaching of His gospel, and I support the mission of taking the Word of God to all nations. I believe the Church has a responsibility to spread the message of salvation, hope, love and repentance. I also believe that those entrusted with leading God's people must be held to a higher standard of conduct, wisdom and integrity.

My faith is not in conflict with my ability to question the conduct of religious leaders. In fact, I believe genuine faith should make us more willing to examine ourselves, confront wrongdoing and distinguish between the Word of God and the personal interests of those who claim to represent Him.

It is against this background that I find some of the reactions by certain pastors to the new restriction on preaching and hawking in moving vehicles troubling. What should have been a reasonable public discussion about law, order, safety and the use of public spaces has, in some quarters, been presented as an attack on the Church and the gospel itself.

But is every regulation that affects a religious activity an attack on Christianity? Must every government policy that inconveniences a pastor be read as persecution? And since when did the gospel become so fragile that a law regulating where and how people conduct their activities could threaten its very existence?

The gospel is sacred, but not every activity conducted in its name is beyond question.

What the regulation actually says

Before anything else, the facts. Regulation 141 of the Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519) prohibits preaching and hawking inside public or commercial vehicles while they are in motion. The penalty is a fine of 10 to 50 penalty units, which the press has put at GH¢120 to GH¢600, imprisonment for up to eight months, or both.

Three things are worth noticing. First, it applies to everyone. The same provision covers the trader selling goods on a moving bus and the preacher with a Bible in the aisle. Second, it does not touch preaching in churches, at crusade grounds, in markets or at lorry parks. It concerns the moving vehicle. Third, it is not new. The earlier Road Traffic Regulations, 2012 (L.I. 2180) carried a similar prohibition. What changed in recent weeks was enforcement.

The reaction was swift. One prominent pastor told his congregation that the restriction was an attempt to gag the church. A pastor who is also a Member of Parliament appealed to the President to scrap what he called a bogus regulation that would jail innocent pastors and evangelists. On 9 October, the President responded that it is not true that the government has banned preaching in vehicles. No one, of any faith, may preach or sell in a moving vehicle, he said, but they may do so when it is stationary. The government has since reportedly suspended implementation, although the details of the suspension remain unclear.

Suspension may calm the temperature. It does not settle the principle, and the principle is what I want to address.

God is a God of order

One of the things that makes some of these arguments difficult to understand is that the Bible itself places considerable emphasis on order. In 1 Corinthians 14:40, Paul instructs believers to let everything be done decently and in order. He was speaking about the gathered church, but the principle reaches beyond the four walls. It speaks to the broader Christian responsibility to conduct ourselves in ways that respect others and reflect the character of the God we serve.

If God values order, why should Christians automatically resist reasonable attempts to regulate activities that affect public safety, traffic, noise, movement and the peaceful use of public spaces?

We cannot insist that society must respect the Church while dismissing the legitimate interests of other members of that same society. Drivers, passengers, pedestrians, traders, workers and residents also have rights. A preacher's desire to win souls does not erase the right of others to travel safely, conduct their business or enjoy a public space without undue interference.

Indeed, if we believe that human life is sacred, then safety regulations should concern us. If we believe that God expects us to love our neighbours, then we must consider how our actions affect them. And if we believe in order, we should be prepared to demonstrate it in our public conduct.

The question, therefore, should not be whether the government has the right to attack the gospel. It should be whether the particular law is reasonable, lawful, proportionate and necessary to address the problem it seeks to solve. That is where an intelligent discussion ought to begin.

When regulation becomes persecution

Some pastors have interpreted the restriction as an attempt to suppress Christianity. Others have extended the argument to include other religious groups, suggesting a wider attack on religious practice. I find this approach deeply problematic.

A law regulating hawking or preaching in moving vehicles does not automatically amount to a prohibition on evangelism. A restriction on the place or manner in which a person conducts an activity is not necessarily a restriction on the belief that motivates it. There is a difference between preventing someone from preaching the gospel and regulating the circumstances under which that preaching takes place.

Ghana's Constitution draws the same line. Article 21(1)(c) guarantees the freedom to practise any religion and to manifest that practice. But Article 12(2) says that the fundamental rights and freedoms in the same chapter are enjoyed subject to respect for the rights and freedoms of others and for the public interest. Religious freedom is real, and it is not unlimited permission to do whatever one wishes in any public space.

If a law genuinely discriminates against Christians, or prohibits them from practising their faith while allowing comparable activities by others, then the Church has every right to raise concerns. But such concerns must be established through evidence and careful reading of the law, not through emotional appeals designed to provoke fear among believers. We must be careful not to turn every disagreement with public policy into a spiritual battle between God and government.

Such language can be particularly powerful in religious settings, because many believers trust their pastors and are reluctant to question their interpretations. When a pastor declares that a government action is an attack on God, some members may accept that conclusion without examining the facts. Others may feel guilty for supporting a law their religious leaders have condemned. Still others may become hostile towards public officials simply because they have been told that their actions threaten the Church.

This is where the misuse of faith becomes dangerous. The pulpit should help people develop spiritual discernment, not discourage them from thinking critically. The gospel should enlighten the conscience, not frighten people into accepting every opinion expressed by a religious leader.

Why drag other religions into the argument?

I am equally concerned about attempts to turn this discussion into a debate about how other religious groups worship. Why should a conversation about the regulation of a particular activity become an opportunity to question the practices of people of different faiths?

Ghana is a religiously diverse country. Christians, Muslims and people of other religious convictions live, work and conduct their affairs alongside one another. Our constitutional commitment to freedom of religion means we must respect the right of others to practise their faith, subject to the law.

The danger of bringing other religions into this debate without a clear reason is that it shifts attention from the legal question to religious rivalry. It can encourage suspicion, deepen divisions and create the impression that public regulation is a contest over which religion has greater influence. That is a dangerous direction for a country such as Ghana.

The proper question is whether the law is fair, whether it serves a legitimate public purpose and whether it respects the rights of everyone affected by it. If it is discriminatory, challenge the discrimination. If it is unreasonable, explain why. If it is poorly drafted, call for clarification or amendment. But do not turn a discussion about public order into an invitation to disparage the beliefs of others. Religious freedom cannot be meaningful if we defend it only when our own religious interests are involved.

Why the law deserves serious consideration

I believe the restriction deserves serious consideration because a moving vehicle is not a conventional place of worship. It is part of a transport system in which safety must take priority. Anything that distracts the driver, crowds the aisle, or exposes passengers to avoidable risk while the vehicle is moving deserves to be regulated, whether it is selling, preaching or anything else. The President's clarification that preaching remains permitted when the vehicle is stationary shows that the target is the movement, not the message.

There must also be room to distinguish between preaching that causes a public nuisance and preaching that is done peacefully without interfering with anyone's rights. A reasonable law should be applied fairly and proportionately, and on that point, I think the critics have a fair question. The aim of the regulation is legitimate. Whether a prison term of up to eight months for a person who preaches on a bus is a proportionate way to achieve it is a different matter, and one on which reasonable people, including Christians who support the regulation's purpose, can disagree. A fine, a warning, or simply a requirement to stop when the bus moves may protect road safety just as well.

That is the kind of argument I would welcome from the pulpit: specific, evidence-based and respectful of the law's purpose. It is a very different thing from claiming that the government is fighting God.

My position is simple. The gospel must be preached, but the preaching of the gospel does not remove the need for public safety, lawful conduct and consideration for others. We cannot claim that our mission is to save lives while behaving carelessly towards the lives of those around us.

Why don't we preach in moving aeroplanes?

I have a question for the pastors who have presented restrictions on preaching in moving vehicles as an attack on the gospel. When you travel on a commercial aeroplane, why don't you stand up and preach to all the passengers?

You may spend several hours on that flight. You may watch a film, listen to music, read a book or talk to the person beside you. Yet how often do you insist that the entire aircraft must become your congregation because you have a divine mandate to preach the Word? Why don't you demand the right to take over the public address system and preach from take-off to landing?

The answer should be obvious. An aeroplane operates under safety procedures and rules designed to protect everyone on board. The fact that a person is a pastor does not exempt him from the arrangements governing the flight. Watching a film does not mean that every other activity must be permitted, and permission to do one thing does not create an unrestricted right to do another.

The point is not that a road vehicle and an aeroplane are identical. They are not. The point is that the setting in which an activity takes place matters. Safety, the rights of other passengers and the rules governing a particular environment cannot be dismissed because someone wishes to carry out a religious activity. If we understand that principle when we travel by air, why does it suddenly become hard to understand when public authorities regulate activities on our roads?

Why don't we preach in banking halls?

Let me ask another question. Why don't pastors walk into banking halls and begin preaching to customers waiting to transact business?

After all, a bank is full of people. Some may be worried about their finances, some may be going through personal difficulties, and some may need hope and the message of salvation. If the presence of people who need the gospel were enough to justify preaching anywhere, why should a banking hall be excluded? Why don't we insist that every bank allow pastors to preach to customers in the queue?

The reason is that a banking hall has a specific purpose. People go there to conduct financial transactions, and the institution has responsibilities for security, privacy, orderly service and the protection of customers. A pastor's good intentions do not automatically override those responsibilities. A person may have a genuine desire to share the gospel and still need to consider whether the place and manner are appropriate.

The same reasoning applies to hospitals, courtrooms, classrooms and offices. Religious expression matters, but it must be weighed alongside the rights and legitimate interests of others. If we accept these boundaries in other settings, we should be able to discuss similar boundaries in public transport without immediately invoking persecution.

The problem of religious blackmail

What troubles me most is the tendency to use the gospel as a shield against reasonable questions and public accountability.

I use the word blackmail deliberately, and I am describing a tactic, not condemning any individual. When a religious leader suggests that questioning his position amounts to fighting God, he is asking for an authority that no human being should possess. When disagreement with a pastor is presented as hostility towards Christianity, the discussion stops being about the merits of an argument. It becomes an attempt to silence criticism through fear. It places believers in a difficult position: agree with the pastor or risk being seen as an enemy of the gospel. It discourages honest discussion and allows personal opinions to take on the appearance of divine instruction.

But a pastor is still a human being. Pastors can misunderstand laws, make poor arguments, pursue personal interests and respond emotionally to criticism. Their positions should be examined with the same care we apply to the claims of politicians, public officials and other leaders. The title of pastor does not make every opinion correct. A pulpit does not turn an interpretation into scripture. And the ability to quote the Bible does not mean that every argument made in its name is sound.

The Church must be especially careful here, because religious leaders hold considerable influence over people who trust them. That influence must be exercised responsibly. We should be able to ask a pastor why he holds a particular position without being made to feel that we have offended God. We should be able to disagree with a religious leader without being threatened with spiritual consequences for questioning his legal or political opinions. Faith should produce discernment, humility and responsibility. It should not become a tool for protecting leaders from scrutiny.

Let us practise what we preach

I stand with the gospel any day. I support the preaching of Jesus Christ and the mission of taking His message to all nations. I believe the Church has a vital role in shaping moral values, offering hope and calling society to righteousness. But I also believe that those who preach the gospel must be willing to live by the principles they teach.

If we preach humility, let us be humble enough to listen to arguments that challenge our views. If we preach truth, let us represent the law accurately. If we preach love, let us consider the rights and safety of people who do not share our faith. If we preach order, let us stop behaving as though rules should apply to everyone except religious leaders. And if we preach wisdom, let us reason before we react.

The Church must not confuse its mission with the personal preferences of its leaders. A regulation affecting a particular activity does not automatically threaten Christianity. If a law is unjust, let us demonstrate its injustice. If it infringes on religious freedom, let us make that case with facts, sound legal reasoning and constitutional principles. If it is reasonable, let us have the courage to acknowledge that, even when it places limits on activities some of us would prefer to conduct without restriction.

There is no shame in a pastor admitting that a law serves a legitimate public purpose. There is no loss of faith in acknowledging that the rights of others matter. And there is no betrayal of the gospel in insisting that religious leaders should act responsibly. What we must stop doing is using the name of God to frighten people into agreement, presenting every disagreement as persecution, and dragging the gospel into controversies that can be settled by reasoned discussion.

Christianity does not need manipulation to survive. The truth does not need intimidation to defend itself.

I will continue to stand for Jesus Christ, for the preaching of His gospel and for the freedom to practise my faith. But I will also stand for reason, public order, fairness and accountability. I will question religious leaders when I believe they are wrong, just as I will question political leaders and public officials when they abuse their positions. My Christianity does not require me to surrender my judgement to another human being.

Let us preach the gospel. Let us win souls. Let us defend religious freedom. But let us also respect the law, consider the rights of others and be honest about our motives. And above all, let us stop pretending that every criticism of a pastor is an attack on God, stop using the gospel to blackmail believers into silence, and start practising what the Bible teaches.

The gospel deserves to be preached with conviction, defended with wisdom and lived with integrity.

Dr Michael Kubi is a lecturer at the University of Professional Studies, Accra, a governance consultant and an author.

Ghana News.title: JoyNews’ Jacqueline Ansomah Yeboah selected for UK Media Excellence for Emerging Technology Fellowship
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews journalist and digital content creator Jacqueline Ansomah Yeboah has been selected for the UK Media Excellence for Emerging Technology (UK MEET) Fellowship, a programme designed to strengthen journalists’ ability to report on emerging technologies and their impact on society.

The fellowship, delivered by Imperial College London through Imperial Global Ghana with support from the British High Commission, brings together journalists to engage with researchers, examine technological claims and develop evidence-led stories on science, technology and innovation.

Jacqueline was selected from a pool of more than 500 applicants from Ghana and Nigeria, with approximately 13 per cent of applicants accepted into the programme.

The residential programme, running from October 11 to 17, 2026, in Accra, focuses on helping journalists interrogate claims about emerging technologies, assess evidence and communicate complex scientific developments in ways that are accessible and relevant to the public.

For Jacqueline, the fellowship presents an opportunity to strengthen her reporting on artificial intelligence and its growing influence on public life, particularly education.

One of her proposed investigations examines whether AI-powered learning tools being introduced into Ghana’s Senior High School education system are improving learning outcomes and whether students across different communities are benefiting equally.

The proposed story seeks to move beyond claims about the potential of artificial intelligence to examine what the evidence shows about its performance in classrooms, how teachers and students use the tools, and whether differences in access to devices, connectivity and digital support affect the benefits students receive.

The investigation would draw on the experiences of students and teachers, alongside insights from independent researchers, technology developers and education authorities.

Yeboah’s approach reflects a central question in technology reporting: how can journalists independently test claims about innovation and explain what the findings mean for the people expected to use it?

The fellowship also provides opportunities for journalists to collaborate with researchers and fellow media professionals, develop story ideas and explore how emerging technologies can be reported responsibly.

As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly prominent in education, healthcare and other sectors, evidence-led journalism will be important in helping the public understand both the opportunities and limitations of these technologies.

Jacqueline Ansomah Yeboah is a journalist and digital content creator with JoyNews, where she works on public-interest reporting, digital storytelling and explainers.

Jacqueline is among five JoyNews journalists selected for the programme. The others are Clinton Yeboah, Emmanule Bright Quaicoe, Blessed Sogah, and Mahmud -Mohammed-Nurudeen.

In all, 30 Ghanaians were selected for the programme.

Ghana News.title: Mental Health Alliance urges government to operationalise Mental Health Fund
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Alliance for Mental Health and Development has called on the government to operationalise the Mental Health Fund established under Section 82 of the Mental Health Act, 2012 (Act 846), to improve the financing of mental healthcare in the country.

The Fund was established to provide sustainable financing for mental healthcare delivery, improve psychiatric infrastructure, support mental health research and promote the welfare of patients and healthcare workers.

However, the Alliance says the Fund has remained dormant since its establishment in 2012, despite the growing need for investment in mental health services.

It is urging the government and relevant stakeholders to take urgent steps to activate the Fund, arguing that the country’s mental healthcare system is facing significant challenges.

The Alliance believes operationalising the Fund would provide a sustainable source of financing for mental healthcare delivery and strengthen efforts to address mental health challenges.

The call was contained in a communiqué signed by Peter Badimak Yaro, National Convenor of the Ghana Alliance for Mental Health and Development, to commemorate World Mental Health Day 2026, under the theme “Lived Experiences Heard, Real Voices, Real Change”.

“While the Mental Health Alliance commends the Government of Ghana for including four mental health conditions on the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), we call on the government to significantly improve financing for mental health through actualising the Mental Health Fund and adequately resourcing it through domestic resource mobilisation. Doing this will bring about full implementation of the Mental Health Law”, the communiqué stated.

Alliance proposes 5% employment quota for persons with disabilities

The Alliance has also proposed that the government reserve a 5% employment quota in local government institutions for persons with disabilities.

It said the proposed policy should be supported by clear implementation and monitoring procedures to ensure that eligible persons benefit.

The Alliance further called on Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) to ensure that the 5% allocation of the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF) is used effectively to equip beneficiaries, including persons with physical, mental and psychosocial disabilities, with employable skills and support for income-generating activities.

“Similarly, we call for increased employment of persons with disabilities, especially young people and females in the corporate and private sectors. These will be realised if the Ghana Labour Law and Disability Law are fully implemented”, the Alliance stressed.

Call to end stigma and discrimination

The Alliance called for increased advocacy by stakeholders to eliminate social stigma, prejudice, stereotypes and discrimination against persons with disabilities.

It also urged stakeholders to promote the participation of persons with disabilities and those who have recovered from mental health conditions in socioeconomic, civic and political activities.

“In particular, people with disabilities and lived experience of mental health conditions must be included as key decision-makers in designing programmes and services planned to support them”, the communiqué stated.

The Alliance stressed that people with disabilities and those with lived experience of mental health conditions should have a meaningful role in shaping the policies and services intended to support them.

Alliance urges responsible media reporting and public accountability

The Alliance said the media had a special responsibility to educate the public about mental health and disability while helping to combat stigma.

It urged media practitioners to use respectful language and protect the dignity and privacy of persons with lived experience of mental health conditions.

It also appealed to journalists to avoid sensationalism and adopt responsible, rights-based reporting on disability and mental health issues.

The Alliance proposed partnerships between the media and civil society organisations to produce educational materials and organise campaigns to promote inclusion and challenge stigma.

“Partnerships with civil society and the Creative Industry could support documentaries, short films and public education campaigns that challenge stigma, and hold institutions accountable for their commitments”, the Alliance stated.

Alliance calls for measurable results

The Alliance called on the Ministry of Finance, the Administrator of the DACF and MMDAs to strengthen transparency and accountability in disability-related funding.

It also urged relevant local government institutions to operationalise inclusive employment measures to improve access to jobs and economic opportunities for persons with disabilities.

National planning and employment agencies, it said, should integrate disability and mental health inclusion into development programmes.

Development partners, foundations and private businesses were also encouraged to invest in inclusive employment, community-based mental health services, legal accountability and sustained anti-stigma campaigns.

“We cannot continue to celebrate commitments while people remain excluded from jobs, essential services and decisions that affect their lives. Inclusion must be reflected in budgets, employment opportunities, accessible services and measurable results,” the Mental Health Alliance stated.

The Alliance reiterated that persons with disabilities and those with lived experience of mental health conditions must not merely be consulted but must meaningfully influence the policies, programmes and resources designed to support them.

Ghana News.title: Ghana–Holy See agreement heads to Parliament after Cabinet approval
Ghana News.content:
Cabinet has approved a longstanding Host Country Agreement between Ghana and the Holy See, clearing the way for its submission to Parliament for ratification.

Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced the decision on Friday, October 9, 2026, during a meeting with the Apostolic Nuncio to Ghana, Archbishop Julien Kaboré.

The agreement seeks to set out the framework governing relations between the two parties, including provisions on special rights, privileges and immunities for ecclesiastical officeholders and Catholic faithful in Ghana.

Mr Ablakwa said the agreement aligns with the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations and addresses an outstanding issue between the Ghanaian government and the Apostolic Nunciature.

He praised officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for their efforts in advancing the agreement and acknowledged the support of President John Dramani Mahama and the Attorney-General in bringing the process to this stage.

Following Cabinet’s approval, Parliament is expected to consider the agreement for ratification under Article 75 of the 1992 Constitution.

Ghana’s formal diplomatic relationship with the Holy See predates the arrival of the country’s first Apostolic Nuncio in 1976.

Mr Ablakwa also recognised the Catholic Church’s contribution to national development, highlighting its work in education and healthcare through institutions serving communities across Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Luv FM Corporate Games 2026: Kumasi Central Prisons, Amanfiman Bank win big amid fun
Ghana News.content:
Corporate institutions in the Ashanti Region gathered for yet another thrilling and energetic day at the Luv FM Corporate Games 2026.

The event brought together more than 22 corporate institutions for sporting activities aimed at promoting physical fitness, workplace relationships and business networking.

Activities on the day included football, volleyball, basketball, table tennis, Ludo, sack bag races, line-and-spoon races and penalty kicks for chief executives of participating companies.

The event saw the Kumasi Central Prisons team emerging overall winners of the much-anticipated 2026 football competition.

The team attributed their victory to discipline, determination and tactical changes during the match.

Speaking after the victory, leader of the group, Deputy Superintendent of Prisons, Richmond Oppong, said the players remained focused despite having only three days of training ahead of the competition.

He indicated that the team’s defensive discipline and strategic substitutions to overpower their opponents saw them perform peerlessly and tactically on the field despite locking horns with Rango Construction Limited.

“The main strategy for us was dedication and the referee was our challenge, but we still managed to secure the win,” he said.

DSP Oppong further expressed excitement about the achievement and confidence in defending the trophy in future editions.

Other winners of the day's activities included Amenfiman Community Bank, which won the table tennis and volleyball competitions, while GLICO emerged winners of the line-and-spoon race and draft competition. CKM won the chief executives' penalty kicks contest.

Marketing and Relationship Manager at the Kumasi Unit of the Multimedia Group Limited, Maxwell Frimpong Manso, said the initiative was designed to encourage workers to stay physically active.

He also highlighted that the event created opportunities for businesses to build relationships and explore partnerships outside their usual work environment.

He further commended the sponsors and partners for supporting the event through funding, products, refreshments and other services, while encouraging more businesses to participate in future editions.

“We appreciate several businesses also supporting the event through sponsorship, refreshments, products and other services,” he noted.

Participating businesses also described the games as a valuable platform for promoting their products and services, increasing brand visibility and engaging potential customers.

They said the event created opportunities to introduce new products, generate customer interest and establish business connections.

The businesses were optimistic that the games would provide more opportunities for corporate engagement, product promotion and business-to-business partnerships.

The Luv FM Corporate Games form part of the station’s efforts to bring corporate institutions together through sports, recreation and networking while providing businesses with opportunities to connect with wider audiences.

The event received support from several corporate partners and sponsors, including Meera Company Limited, BonAgro Limited, Conkfans Company Limited, General Dentessa Limited, Mid City Dental Clinic, and Coca-Cola.

Others are Ecobank, Royal Basin Hotel, Amenfiman Community Bank, Oak Specialist Hospital, Medimoses Day-to-Day Eye Clinic, Optimal Medical Diagnosis, Rango Construction Limited, and Astolinks.

Ghana News.title: WAFU B U17: Ghana top Group A after win over Togo
Ghana News.content:
The Black Starlets have moved to the top of Group A at the 2026 WAFU Zone B U-17 Championship following their 1-0 victory over Togo on Saturday in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.

David Kwarteng scored the decisive goal in the seventh minute at the August 4 Sports Stadium to hand the Black Starlets all three points in their opening fixture of the competition, which serves as the qualifying tournament for the 2027 U-17 Africa Cup of Nations.

The result puts Ghana in a strong position in Group A after hosts Burkina Faso and Benin played out a goalless draw in the other opening-day encounter.

Ghana lead the group with three points, while Burkina Faso and Benin have one point each, with Togo yet to register a point.

The team will face Benin on Tuesday, October 13, in their second Group A match, seeking another positive result to strengthen their position in the race for a place at the 2027 U-17 AFCON.

Ghana News.title: Ho Central Mosque reopens amid unresolved leadership dispute that led to closure
Ghana News.content:
Women of Zongo Community in Aflao participated in the advocacy workshop

The leadership dispute that led to violent clashes and a shooting incident at the Ho Central Mosque in the Volta region remains unresolved, despite the reopening of the worship space after months of closure.

Thirteen people were injured in the shooting, which occurred during clashes over the regional Islamic leadership position and resulted in the indefinite closure of the mosque.

The National Chief Imam reopened the mosque on Saturday, October 10, 2026, allowing Muslims in Ho Zongo to return for worship. However, concerns persist over the underlying disagreement and the need to prevent further violence.

Ho Zongo youth leader Mohammed Salisu Kidzah welcomed the reopening but demanded accountability for the shooting.

Speaking to Citi News, he said residents celebrated the restoration of access to the mosque, although their pursuit of justice would continue.

“We are happy for the reopening. There were a lot of people here in the morning celebrating the reopening,” he said.

Mr Kidzah urged the authorities to ensure that those responsible for the shooting face the law, warning that leaving the matter unresolved could undermine peace in the community.

He alleged that the shooting incident was not the first time at the mosque and stressed the need to address the recurring tensions.

“We want peace, and the National Chief Imam called for peace when he was here,” he said.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
