Erling Haaland said Manchester City’s 3-0 win at 10-man Liverpool showed they will “stick together” after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

Haaland put City ahead at Anfield on Sunday before Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki netted to silence Anfield after Liverpool fans barraged them with taunts about the guilty verdict.

Enzo Maresca’s side showed no signs of being fazed by the abuse in their first match since the club discovered an independent commission had found them guilty of breaking over 100 financial regulations.

City, who are appealing against the decision, could face a massive points deduction that would likely lead to relegation or even be stripped of their titles.

But for now Norway striker Haaland insisted their defiant performance at old rivals Liverpool proved they are still committed to the City cause.

“Every single person that is part of Man City, and every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time,” he said.

“It was hard, but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone. It’s always tough to come here.

“Important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That’s the only thing we can do.”

City were helped by Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch’s red card for two bookings just prior to Haaland’s opener.

They ran riot after that to move three points clear at the top of the Premier League.

Whether they are able to maintain a title challenge with a potential punishment looming remains to be seen.

Haaland said City’s players can only concentrate on their performances while the club’s Abu Dhabi-based owners deal with the legal ramifications of the verdict.

“You want to win games, it’s as simple as that. Perform well, play good football and win games. This was a mental battle,” he said.

“Proud that we managed to stick together, we are mentally strong. Plenty of games coming up so time to recover and go again.”

City midfielder Elliot Anderson delivered a composed display in his first taste of the rivalry with Liverpool after his close-season move from Nottingham Forest.

The England international echoed Haaland’s assessment of his side’s spirit, saying: “Togetherness, fight, a tough place to come and we stuck together and fought for each other. We’ve showed courage.

“The atmosphere was more than normal, arriving into Anfield and the first 10 minutes of the game.

“We did well to quieten the crowd. Struggled first half but second we were better and then the goals came.”

World.title: Zelensky says Russia hit power plant ‘after’ Trump’s energy ceasefire announcement
World.content:
Zelensky

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday that Russia had attacked an energy plant after US President Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” between the two countries.

“The Russians struck a power plant in Kyiv with a ‘shahed’ drone,” Zelensky said in a social media post, adding that strikes on other energy facilities followed in the Kharkiv region.

“And all of this happened AFTER the President of the United States made his statement about an energy ceasefire,” he added.

Earlier Sunday, US President Donald Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt strikes on each other’s energy infrastructure.

Zelensky was quick to say this was news to him and there has so far been no response from Moscow.

Vanguard News

World.title: Petrol: Marketers hike pump price in Abuja, Lagos by N29/litre
World.content:
By Udeme Akpan & Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

Days after the Federal Government announced measures to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices on consumers, petroleum marketers have increased petrol pump prices by up to N29 per litre in Abuja.

Checks across the nation’s capital on Sunday showed that AA Rano and AYM Shafa increased their pump prices to N1,409 per litre from N1,380 per litre last week.

Similarly, an NNPC Retail outlet in Azhata, Jikwoyi District, increased its pump price to N1,405 per litre from N1,380, while MRS, a partner retail outlet of Dangote Refinery, raised its price to N1,405 per litre from N1,370.

The increases came despite the Federal Government’s petrol discount initiative, under which the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) extended its N66-per-litre discount until October 31, 2026.

The discount, introduced on October 1 to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary, reduced NNPC Retail’s N1,405 pump price to N1,339 per litre for customers who pay digitally through its mobile application.

The Federal Government said the initiative was being funded through NNPC Retail’s decision to forgo its profit margin rather than through public funds, stressing that it did not amount to a return to petrol subsidy.

In Lagos, some stations in Ikorodu and other locations sold petrol at N1,360 per litre, while outlets in Coker, Orile and Second Rainbow retailed the product at N1,350 per litre.

However, some independent oil marketers sold petrol at between N1,360 and N1,400 per litre, depending on location.

The latest increases reflect continuing pressure on domestic petrol prices following the rise in global crude oil prices amid the Middle East conflict.

In a statement, NNPC Limited said its discount was intended to provide relief to consumers during the period of elevated global market uncertainty.

It stated: “We recognise that higher petrol prices affect everyday life, from the cost of commuting to the expenses of running a business. We understand the strain on families and livelihoods, and this discount is intended to provide direct relief to customers during this difficult period.

“Following the statement by the Honourable Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, on 8 October 2026, NNPC Limited reiterates its commitment to working with the government and stakeholders to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices on households, businesses and the wider economy.

“Before the announcement, NNPC Limited had introduced a sales discount on 1 October 2026 to commemorate Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary. This will now continue until 31 October 2026 across NNPC Retail stations nationwide. This discount is a customer relief initiative and does not represent the reintroduction of petroleum subsidy.

“This initiative supports the government’s responsible and proactive approach to providing practical relief to Nigerians during a period of heightened global market uncertainty. The initiative applies to NNPC Retail outlets and does not establish a uniform national pump price or alter the market-based pricing framework applicable to petroleum products.

“NNPC Limited remains committed to reliable product supply and collaboration with the government and stakeholders to help ease the burden on Nigerians. We therefore urge the public to disregard any interpretation of this discount as a subsidy restoration.”

It added: “We appreciate Nigerians’ continued patronage and support, and remain committed to clear communication about our products, prices and customer initiatives.”

World.title: ADC campaign to police: You can’t arrest hunger by stopping rally
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has accused the Kano State Police Command of suppressing dissent after operatives allegedly disrupted a ‘Tinubu Must Go’ rally and arrested the owner of the venue where it was held.

The council said the incident at The Avenue Event Center, Kano, exposed the tension between the government’s democratic claims and citizens’ right to protest, warning that police action could neither silence public frustration nor erase anger over hunger, insecurity and the rising cost of living.

In a statement on Sunday by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the council said the rally, led by Barrister Abba Hikima and organised by concerned youths, was disrupted when police operatives barricaded the venue and allegedly intimidated participants.

“This is not democracy. This is tyranny. For how long will the APC continue to use the police to suppress dissenting voices?” Ologbondiyan queried.

The ADC-PCC expressed particular outrage over the reported arrest of the event centre owner for allegedly allowing the gathering, questioning why a business owner should face arrest for providing a venue for a peaceful assembly.

“The message from Kano is loud and clear: Nigerians are tired, hungry and angry. You can stop a rally and arrest a venue owner, but you cannot arrest hunger in the land. You cannot barricade the anger and frustration of over 200 million people,” Ologbondiyan said.

The council accused the APC-led government of misdirecting its priorities, arguing that the effort deployed to stop the rally should instead be channelled into tackling insecurity, banditry and the cost-of-living crisis.

“If the APC government had deployed the same energy it used to stop a peaceful rally at The Avenue Event Center to tackle insecurity, banditry and the excruciating cost of living, Nigeria would be a safer and more prosperous nation,” he added.

The ADC-PCC commended Hikima and the participating youths for standing their ground despite the reported police intimidation. It also urged the Inspector-General of Police and the Kano State Police Command to ensure the immediate and unconditional release of the venue owner, if still in custody, and refrain from actions that could turn the police into an instrument of political oppression.

The council further called on civil society organisations, human rights groups and the international community to monitor what it described as an erosion of democratic freedoms.

“The right to protest is not a privilege granted by the police or the APC; it is a right guaranteed by the Constitution. No amount of intimidation will stop Nigerians from demanding change,” the statement said.

World.title: 2027: Enugu Govt alleges opposition plot to import armed thugs, bandits
World.content:
Gov Peter Mbah of Enugu State.

…Denies government involvement in NDC airport, secretariat incidents

Says Mbah’s performance more than enough to win free, fair election

The Enugu State Government said it has uncovered alleged plans by some opposition elements to import armed thugs and bandits into the state to create panic and a false sense of insecurity ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Prof. Chidiebere Onyia, made these known on Sunday while addressing a press conference at the Government House, Enugu, on the incidents involving the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport and the party’s state secretariat in Enugu on Saturday.

Onyia denied any involvement of the government or the Governor’s Chief Security Officer, Ifeanyi Osondu, in both incidents, describing the airport confrontation as a matter between the NDC and federal authorities, while noting that the shooting incident at the party’s secretariat was under police investigation.

According to the SSG, the government’s preliminary findings indicated that the airport incident followed the NDC’s attempt to hold what it described as a “Grand Statewide Campaign Flag-off 2026” at the facility without securing the necessary approval from the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN).

He said the party had published notices inviting its members and supporters to the event, including on the Facebook page of its governorship candidate in the state.

Onyia explained that the police had advised the party to obtain FAAN’s approval before security personnel could be deployed to the airport for the event.

“Further findings, however, revealed that the NDC did not secure the approval of FAAN to host a grand statewide rally at its facility. Security agencies, therefore, advised the organisers of the rally to rethink it,” he said.

The SSG alleged that the party proceeded to mobilise its members to the airport and attempted to gain entry into the facility, resulting in a confrontation with airport authorities.

He said security agencies intervened to disperse the “riotous” party members and restore order around the airport, which he described as a strategic national asset.

Onyia added that the state government’s account was consistent with the statement issued by the Enugu State Police Command on Sunday.

NDC Secretariat Shooting

On the shooting incident at the NDC state secretariat in the GRA area of Enugu, the SSG said security reports had established that a violent clash occurred at the party’s office and that the police were investigating the matter.

The SSG disputed reports alleging fatalities, stating that the government’s findings indicated that no death had occurred in the incident.

He disclosed that a 43-year-old man, identified as Ifeanyi Nworie, sustained a gunshot wound and was taken to the Enugu State University Teaching Hospital, Park Lane, where he was stabilised before being transferred to the National Orthopaedic Hospital, Enugu, for further examination.

“We can, therefore, authoritatively report that there were no deaths as falsely claimed by some reports and NDC leaders,” he said.

Onyia also faulted allegations that the Governor’s Chief Security Officer was present at the party secretariat and supervised the shooting, maintaining that the official was with Governor Peter Mbah at the Teachers Grassroots Movement mega rally at Okpara Square, Enugu, at the time of the incident.

The SSG further criticised the reported holding of a minute’s silence for an individual he said was still alive, describing it as an attempt to mislead the public for political advantage.

Reaffirming the state government’s position, Onyia said Governor Mbah had sworn to protect the lives and property of all residents, irrespective of their religious beliefs or political affiliations, and condemned.

He said the administration’s ambition to grow Enugu into a $30 billion economy and make it a preferred destination for investment, business, tourism and living depended significantly on sustained peace and security.

According to him, this informed the government’s substantial investments in security infrastructure and operations over the past three years.

“Consequently, the Enugu State Government strongly condemns in its entirety any form of violence, including politically induced violence in the state. We welcome healthy debate and freedom of association and peaceful assembly,” he said.

He, however, urged political parties and their candidates to exercise restraint and embrace issue-based campaigns ahead of the 2027 elections.

The SSG said democratic rights should be exercised responsibly, arguing that political parties ought to serve as models of decorum and integrity.

He questioned the decision to announce a statewide campaign flag-off at the airport and without the approval of the relevant authorities.

“Without holding brief for FAAN, is it not sheer rascality to attempt to hold a “Grand Statewide Campaign Flag-off 2026” of the NDC at the airport as publicised by the party and its gubernatorial candidate, especially without the approval by the appropriate authorities?

“Is it not equally gross mischief and a sign of political desperation to hold a minute silence for a living person, just to mislead the public for political traction?” he queried.

Onyia accused opposition elements in the state of attempting to create the impression that Enugu was unsafe and that the government was intolerant of opposing political parties.

He alleged that some opposition groups had been attributing internal disagreements and violent clashes to the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state.

As an example, he cited the September 12, 2026 incident at Obuofia in Nkanu West Local Government Area, claiming that investigations had identified the alleged perpetrators, who were being prosecuted by the police.

The SSG described the opposition as factionalised and alleged that some of its members were seeking to draw the state government into controversies for political relevance.

Onyia also reiterated the government’s allegation that some opposition elements were plotting to bring armed thugs and bandits into Enugu to create panic and undermine public confidence in the state’s security ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“We, however, make bold to say that the peace and security we have achieved in Enugu State in the last three years, and at huge material costs and sacrifices by our security agents, are non-negotiable and irreversible,” he said.

The SSG said the Mbah administration remained committed to protecting citizens’ democratic rights, including the freedom to campaign for and vote for candidates of their choice in the forthcoming elections.

He described the right of residents to elect their leaders through free, fair and credible polls as fundamental to the state’s democratic development.

Onyia added that the government was confident of securing a second term for Mbah based on what it described as the governor’s performance and delivery on campaign promises.

“Indeed, these inalienable rights of Ndi Enugu to elect their leaders in free, fair and credible polls are our surest hope for re-election come 2027,” he said.

He added that the administration had no reason to resort to desperate measures, maintaining that its record in office would be the basis for seeking a renewed mandate from the electorate.

World.title: Amnesty condemns police blockade of ‘Tinubu-Must-Go’ event in Kano
World.content:
Amnesty International Nigeria has condemned the alleged blocking of a “Tinubu-Must-Go” event in Kano State, accusing the police of violating the rights to freedom of association and peaceful assembly.

The human rights organisation disclosed this in a post on its X platform on Sunday, saying heavily armed police officers blocked both ends of the road leading to the venue of the event.

Amnesty described the action as an unlawful restriction on peaceful political activities and called on the Nigeria Police Force to desist from what it termed a reckless violation of human rights.

“The Nigeria Police must desist from such reckless violation of human rights. It is perfectly within the rights of supporters of all candidates and all political parties to carry out peaceful political activities,” the organisation said.

It maintained that the police had a responsibility to facilitate peaceful political gatherings, regardless of the political party or candidate being supported or opposed.

“The duty of the police is to facilitate peaceful conduct of such political gatherings — no matter the political party or candidate being supported or opposed,” Amnesty said.

The organisation stressed that freedom of association and peaceful assembly was not exclusive to any political party or its supporters.

It further described the Kano incident as part of what it called a troubling pattern of police repression targeting opposition members in different parts of the country.

According to Amnesty, repeated attacks and intimidation against opposition supporters could undermine their ability to associate freely and organise peaceful public gatherings.

The organisation did not provide further details about the event or the police operation in its post.

World.title: Otti warns Abians against selling future for ₦5,000, rice
World.content:
— Says politicians who ruined state over 24 years are back

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has warned voters against trading the state’s future for paltry financial inducements ahead of the 2027 general elections, cautioning that accepting as little as ₦5,000, ₦10,000, rice or wrappers from politicians could mortgage the state’s destiny for another four years.

Otti, who spoke on Sunday through his Chief of Staff, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, at the Second Session of the Seventh Synod of the Anglican Communion, Aba Ngwa North Diocese, alleged that politicians responsible for Abia’s 24 years of underdevelopment were returning to seek the people’s support.

He urged voters to scrutinise the records and intentions of politicians rather than allow temporary material benefits to influence their choices at the polls.

The synod, held at All Saints Anglican Cathedral, Abayi, Umuocham, Aba, had the theme, “Don’t Just Absorb It; Think It Through,” drawn from Acts 17:11-12.

Warning that the consequences of selling votes could outlast the immediate benefits, Otti said, “Don’t use the ₦5,000, the ₦10,000, the wrapper or the rice they will give you and close the destiny of Abians for the next four years. Even prayer and fasting will not open it.”

He added, “May we not lose what God has given to us on a platter of gold.”

The governor also cautioned Christians against being swayed by politicians who, according to him, had suddenly become attentive to the church and its members as the election season approached.

“Many of them who have not been coming to church have started coming to church. Many of them who have not been accepting or taking your calls have suddenly started calling you. If you call them and you miss their call, they call you back. Those are devices,” he said.

Otti urged the electorate to examine such political overtures critically and make informed decisions about the state’s future.

‘Next four years for consolidation’

The governor said his administration had spent its first three years laying the foundation for Abia’s development, expressing confidence that the next four years, beginning in 2027, would focus on consolidating the gains recorded so far.

“Those who build houses will understand that foundation-laying is the most crucial, and the foundation has been laid after 24 years of ruins,” he said.

According to him, the next phase would bring consolidation and further development, adding that Abia had become a point of reference.

On the church’s development projects, Otti assured the congregation of his administration’s support while reiterating that public funds must be deployed for the overall development of the state rather than individual religious projects.

He also urged Christians to verify information and think critically before reaching conclusions, saying the church had an important role to play in changing the country’s negative narratives.

“Christians, we have the capacity to change the negative narrative of this nation, and especially our state,” he said.

Church leaders preach political discernment

Earlier, the Bishop of Aba Ngwa North Diocese, Rt. Rev. Dr Nathan Kanu, said the synod’s theme challenged Christians to move beyond merely hearing messages to examining issues prayerfully and responding wisely.

Kanu commended Otti for identifying with the church and supporting its activities. He also presented gifts to the governor’s representative and prayed for God’s blessings upon the governor and his administration.

In his sermon, the guest speaker and Bishop of Ohaji/Egbema Diocese, Rt. Rev. Chidi Oparajiaku, urged Christians to examine what they hear before taking action.

Speaking on “The Bereans’ Wisdom,” with texts from Acts 17:12-15, Oparajiaku said the synod’s theme was particularly relevant in the present circumstances.

“It didn’t say throw it away; it says think through it,” he said, regretting that some Christians had become vulnerable to deception because they failed to examine issues in the light of biblical teachings.

“When members of the church know the Bible, they would not be deceived,” he added.

The cleric also thanked God for giving Abia Governor Otti, whom he credited with changing the state’s narrative.

World.title: 2027: Atiku demands names of firms printing INEC’s ballot papers
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disclose who is printing sensitive materials for the 2027 elections, warning that opaque contracts and key departmental redeployments could undermine confidence in the polls.

His central concern is that Nigerians could head into a decisive election without knowing who is producing their ballots, how the contracts were awarded or what safeguards exist against political interference.

In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, for the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku demanded explanations for reported changes in INEC’s Electoral Operations Department and allegations that a substantial share of sensitive election materials had been allocated to private contractors.

Reports indicate that Director Isa Magaji Gum was moved from Electoral Operations to the Voter Registry Department, while Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi was appointed to head Electoral Operations. Dr Lawrence Bayode was also identified as head of Information and Communication Technology.

“These departments are at the heart of election administration. INEC must explain these decisions, publish the criteria applied and show that every appointment and redeployment followed due process, was based on merit and was free from political interference.”

Atiku also demanded that INEC confirm or deny whether Hitech, or any company associated with it, had secured a contract to print sensitive election materials.

He alleged that more than half of the materials, including presidential ballot assets, might have been allocated to an undisclosed company believed to be based in France. He further questioned reports that the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Plc was printing materials for only 15 to 17 states, leaving private firms to handle the remainder.

“Nigerians should not have to depend on unnamed sources to discover who is producing their ballots,” he said, demanding the disclosure of contractors, allocations, procurement methods and security arrangements.

Atiku argued that any contract awarded to Hitech or an associated company would raise questions about INEC’s neutrality, citing publicly reported business ties between the Chagoury family, which owns Hitech, and the Tinubu family.

The former vice-president also pointed to controversy surrounding Hitech contracts under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, including the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway project.

“If neither Hitech nor a company associated with it has been selected, INEC must say so clearly and put the matter beyond doubt,” he said.

He urged the Central Bank of Nigeria to disclose its banknote-printing allocations and explain the roles of domestic and foreign contractors, while calling on INEC to maximise domestic security-printing capacity and ensure every ballot and result sheet is protected by a transparent chain of custody.

Atiku warned that Nigerians battered by economic hardship would resist any attempt to subvert their votes, insisting that the 2027 election must not become an instrument for prolonging the Tinubu administration’s hold on power.

“Let there be no mistake: Nigerians will not accept a stolen election. Any attempt to rig the 2027 polls will be met with determined resistance through the ballot, lawful civic action, and every other democratic channel available to the people.”

He said the ADC would monitor INEC’s preparations and alert domestic and international observers to any lack of transparency, insisting that the commission must prove its impartiality through verifiable disclosures.

World.title: NGX Group’s Push for Local Tech Listings Gains Attention Amid OPay IPO Plans
World.content:
Adeolu Martins

OPay, one of Africa’s leading fintech companies, has secured board and shareholder approval to pursue a secondary listing on Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) following the completion of its planned primary listing on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), a development that aligns with Nigerian Exchange Group Plc’s (NGX Group) earlier advocacy for leading Nigerian businesses to list domestically and expand opportunities for local ownership.

The decision was disclosed in OPay’s Form F-1 registration statement filed with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on October 9, 2026. The company is pursuing an initial public offering (IPO) of American Depositary Shares (ADSs) and has applied to list on the NYSE under the proposed ticker symbol ‘OPAY’. The planned Nigerian listing remains subject to market conditions and applicable regulatory approvals.

The development comes barely two months after the Board and Management of NGX Group, led by its Chairman, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, and Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Temi Popoola, met with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, where they advocated a deliberate national strategy to encourage leading Nigerian businesses, particularly technology companies, to list domestically or pursue dual listings.

During the August 6 engagement, Popoola specifically identified OPay among the major fintech companies whose participation in the domestic capital market could broaden investment opportunities for Nigerians. His proposition was anchored on a broader ambition: ensuring that companies generating significant economic value from Nigeria also provide opportunities for domestic investors to participate in their growth and long-term wealth creation.

Popoola has consistently advocated moving Nigerians beyond their roles as consumers, employees and users of services to become shareholders in the businesses driving economic growth. For a company such as OPay, whose growth is supported by a substantial Nigerian customer base, a domestic listing could provide an opportunity for its users to participate in its ownership and share in the value it creates.

Kwairanga has emphasised the capital market’s role as a critical national platform for financing enterprise, supporting industrialisation and driving inclusive prosperity. From this perspective, attracting leading Nigerian businesses to the Exchange is not merely about increasing listings; it is about mobilising long-term capital to support business growth while strengthening the link between corporate success and national economic development.

OPay’s formal disclosure gives greater substance to this proposition. While its proposed US IPO would provide access to international capital, the planned secondary listing on NGX could establish an additional pathway for Nigerian investors to participate in the company’s growth, bringing domestic ownership into a business with a significant presence in Nigeria’s digital financial services sector.

The potential significance extends beyond OPay. Nigeria has produced several technology-driven businesses with substantial operations, customer bases and economic footprints, yet opportunities for domestic investors to participate in their ownership remain limited. Encouraging these businesses to access the Nigerian capital market could help bridge that gap, deepen market liquidity, broaden the Exchange’s sectoral representation and connect more Nigerians to the wealth generated by the country’s expanding digital economy.

For NGX Group, the development reinforces the relevance of its ongoing engagement with policymakers, regulators and corporate leaders to position the capital market as a central platform for long-term capital formation. The Group’s agenda goes beyond attracting new listings to building a market capable of supporting enterprise growth, mobilising domestic and international capital, and expanding public participation in Nigeria’s economic development.

Although OPay has secured the necessary corporate approvals to pursue a Nigerian listing, the transaction remains contingent on the completion of its NYSE listing and compliance with applicable Nigerian regulatory and market requirements. Nevertheless, the company’s decision brings renewed attention to a central message from NGX Group’s engagement with President Tinubu: Nigeria’s ambition to build a globally competitive economy must be matched by opportunities for Nigerians to invest in the businesses driving that growth.

As more Nigerian-focused companies pursue international expansion and access to global capital, the opportunity is to ensure that their success also translates into broader domestic ownership, deeper capital markets and more inclusive wealth creation.

* Adeolu, a financial market analyst, writes from Lagos

World.title: D-8 Countries Set to Hold International Ministerial Meeting in Ekiti
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado Ekiti

Ekiti State is set to achieve a major international breakthrough as the Developing-8 (D-8) Organisation for Economic Cooperation has selected the state to host its 5th ministerial meeting and 6th Senior Officials’ Meeting scheduled for October 28 to 30, 2026.

The high-level gathering, which will hold at the iconic Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort, is expected to place Ekiti at the centre of global diplomatic and tourism conversations, bringing together ministers, senior government officials and policy experts from some of the world’s emerging economies.

The development represents another major milestone in the state’s growing profile as a tourism destination, investment and international conferences, following sustained efforts by the administration of Governor Biodun Abayomi Oyebanji to reposition Ekiti’s natural, cultural and economic assets for global relevance.

Findings by THISDAY revealed that the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and Creative Economy has commenced preparations for the landmark event, with the Minister, Hannatu Musa Musawa, initiating official engagements with the Ekiti State Government and other critical stakeholders towards ensuring a successful hosting.

The D-8 member countries — Nigeria, Türkiye, Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Iran and Azerbaijan — are expected to converge on Ekiti for discussions centred on economic cooperation, trade, tourism development and sustainable growth.

Beyond the formal ministerial sessions, the programme is expected to feature tourism exhibitions, cultural showcases, investment presentations and guided tours designed to expose delegates to Ekiti’s rich heritage, indigenous cuisine, hospitality industry and investment opportunities.

The choice of Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort, one of Nigeria’s most celebrated tourism destinations, has been described by stakeholders as a significant endorsement of Ekiti’s emergence as a peaceful and attractive destination for meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE).

Industry observers noted that the selection reflects the increasing visibility of the state, driven by investments in infrastructure, security, tourism promotion and policies aimed at improving the ease of doing business.

The transformation of Ekiti’s road network, strengthening of security architecture, aggressive promotion of tourism assets and the completion of the Ekiti Agro-Allied International Cargo Airport have continued to enhance the state’s accessibility and appeal to visitors and investors.

Since commercial flight operations commenced in December 2025, the state has witnessed improved connectivity, providing fresh opportunities for business tourism, conferences and investment engagements.

Ekiti has also continued to attract national recognition for its tourism drive, emerging as Nigeria’s Most Active Tourism State for three consecutive years — a feat that has further strengthened its reputation as one of the country’s fastest-growing tourism destinations.

For the Ekiti State Bureau of Tourism Development, led by Director-General, Ambassador Wale Ojo-Lanre, the D-8 meeting provides another strategic platform to showcase the state’s tourism potentials before an influential global audience and deepen the vision of making tourism a major pillar of economic development.

Beyond the prestige of hosting international dignitaries, the event is expected to generate economic benefits across the hospitality, transportation, entertainment, food, arts and creative sectors, while creating new pathways for investment partnerships and international destination marketing.

Although the Federal Government has not publicly attributed the choice of Ekiti to any specific achievement, the hosting of the D-8 Ministerial Meeting provides the state with a significant opportunity to showcase the impact of its investments in peace, security, infrastructure and tourism development.

World.title: Kwara Central APC Women Hold Rally for AbdulRazaq’s Senatorial Ticket, Other Candidates
World.content:
• Says gov’s gender inclusion policy, other feats will speak for him at polls

Thousands of Kwara Central Women in the All Progressives Congress (APC) on Saturday held a mega rally in Ilorin to mobilise support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and election of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq who is the party’s standard-bearer for Kwara Central Senatorial ticket in the forthcoming general election.

The rally, led by the Senior Special Assistant, Women Mobilization, Hon. Monsurat Abimbola Lawal, kicked off at the General Hospital Roundabout, Ilorin and criss-crossed some major streets of the city, including Surulere, Agaka, Oja Oba market, Gambari, Ita-adu, Kankatu, Omoda and Alore.

The marchers, who were decked in uniform, could not hide their joy as they danced to different pro-APC lyrics while also displaying their various banners.

“This public demonstration is rooted in our love, support and commitment to mobilizing votes for our hard working leader and Governor, Mallam AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, who is contesting for the Senate,” Lawal told reporters on the sidelines of the rally.

“We also staged the rally in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and other APC candidates across the state. And we believe that Kwarans are students of history, who have felt impacts of this government in positive ways. They know the difference between Kwara of yesterday and today. We are confident that they would not make moves that could bring us back. We are indeed going forward.”

She sued for continued peace and unity among party faithful and for an unwavering support for APC candidates across board.

Councilor of Warah-Oshin/Egbejila Ward and Deputy Speaker of Ilorin West Legislative Council, Hon. Sherifat Balogun, for her part, appealed to all aggrieved members of the party to join the moving train in the interest of the state, saying the governor is doing a lot to transform Kwara.

She noted that the APC is in charge of Kwara State, given ‘the organic crowd’ and the massive support the government continues to enjoy from the residents, who she said have seen the difference.

“APC is in charge, as evident in the turnout. We didn’t hire anybody. You can see all of us in uniform. These are just a few of us who came out from Kwara Central, because it’s a voluntary rally. Nobody is paying us for anything,” she said, explaining that the purpose was chiefly to prove the governor’s success story and the feedback from citizens, particularly the people of Kwara Central.

“We are appealing to the aggrieved members to join the moving train for the continuity of good works that the Governor is doing.”

A member from Oloje Ward, Ambassador Zakariya Muminat Jumai, who hailed AbdulRazaq’s commitment to gender inclusion, said the administration continues to empower and give women and youth the opportunity to participate in decision making.

She said: “The major party we have in Kwara is APC. Others are minority and we are majority. We can beat our chest and tell the whole world that APC is 100% in Kwara State, and we guarantee that we will be the winner of the upcoming elections, Insha Allah.

“We just gathered members of APC who are here to display support and promote the candidates. We are here to canvas for them, to let them know the purpose of women, and to let them know the women are behind them.

“We are innovative and we appreciate the governor for motivating us. We have women, who are commissioners, senior special assistants (SSAs) and special assistants (SAs), among others and they are performing creditably well.”

Hajia Falilat Saka (aka Iya Eleja) said the rally was to show solidarity for the candidacy of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, Hon Salihu Yakubu Danladi and all other APC candidates.

“Today’s rally shows that women in Kwara Central and across the state are solidly behind Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, Hon Salihu Yakubu Danladi and other APC candidates, and they would all have the day in the 2027 general election,” she said.

World.title: N69.5m Poster Fine Sparks ADC, Plateau Face-off
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the Plateau State Government have clashed over a N69.5 million fine imposed for alleged violations of Executive Order 003 regulating the display of political posters.

The ADC accused the government and the Jos Metropolitan Development Board (JMDB) of selective enforcement, alleging that while its campaign posters attracted sanctions, posters bearing the images of Governor Caleb Mutfwang and President Bola Tinubu remained visible on public infrastructure.

Addressing journalists in Jos, the party’s state Publicity Secretary, Silas Audu Wettok, demanded the withdrawal or suspension of the fine pending a transparent review, insisting that regulations should be enforced fairly across all political parties.

“Our objection is not to legitimate regulation, but to the apparent selective enforcement of the order,” he said.

The ADC also urged the government to focus more on tackling insecurity, saying the protection of lives and property should receive the same urgency as enforcement actions against political posters.

However, the Plateau State Government dismissed allegations of bias, maintaining that the directive applies to all parties without exception.

General Manager of the Plateau Metropolitan Development Agency, Hart Bankat, said 139 posters were removed from the Secretariat Bridge, attracting fines totalling N69.5 million at N500,000 per poster.

According to him, both the ADC and the All Progressives Congress (APC) have been sanctioned under the same order, adding that evidence exists showing the removal of posters bearing the images of Tinubu and Mutfwang from prohibited locations.

“APC have been fined and ADC have also been fined. It is left for them. The fine is for the good of the Plateau people, not for anything,” Bankat said.

The agency chief further alleged that some ADC posters had been displayed within the premises of a primary school, raising concerns about the use of public facilities for political campaigns.

Bankat warned that campaign and party offices found violating the directive could be sealed off within seven days, stressing that the policy is aimed at protecting public infrastructure and preserving the environment rather than targeting any political group.

The ADC, meanwhile, insisted that the fine would not deter its preparations for future elections and renewed its call for equal treatment of all political parties in the state.

World.title: IGP Visits NAF Hqrs, Commiserates with Air Chief, Families of Deceased Crew Members, Passengers
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, has commiserated with the Nigerian Air Force (NAF), the Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and the families of the deceased crew members and passengers who lost their lives in the ill-fated NAF 931 aircraft crash in Ondo State.

The IGP expressed his condolences during a visit to NAF Headquarters, where he commiserated with the leadership, officers and personnel of the NAF, as well as the families of those who lost their lives in the incident.

He expressed the solidarity of the Nigeria Police Force with the NAF and prayed for strength and comfort for the bereaved families and colleagues of the deceased.

According to a statement by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Anietie Iniedu, the Nigeria Police Force remains in solidarity with the NAF at this difficult time and honours the service and sacrifice of those who lost their lives.

World.title: FRC, Housing Ministry Fret over Poor Pace of Work at Delta Renewed Hope Housing Project
World.content:
Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

The Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC) and the Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development have expressed concern over the slow pace and quality of work at the Renewed Hope Affordable Housing Programme (RHAHP) project located in the Asaba-Uvwie-Ekpan axis of Delta State.

The concern was raised when the FRC South-south Verification Team on Selected Federal Government Projects inspected the 96-unit housing project as part of its ongoing physical verification exercise across the South-south region.

During the inspection, the team observed that only four of the 96 housing units were nearing completion, while several aspects of the project, including roofing and other infrastructure, remained either incomplete or unattended to.

The Team Lead and Head of the Strategic Communications Directorate of the FRC, Mr. Bede Ogueri Anyanwu, expressed concern over the quality and pace of work at the site.

According to him, the Renewed Hope Affordable Housing Programme was conceived as part of the Federal Government’s efforts to improve living conditions and expand access to affordable housing and other essential services for Nigerians.

He noted that the level of work observed at the site did not reflect the objectives of the programme, stressing the need for contractors to return to the site and complete their respective assignments to the required standards.

Anyanwu specifically called for M/s Goodnews Creative Ideas Limited and M/s First Class Capital Project Limited to return to the site and address outstanding works, particularly the roofing of the buildings.

The verification team observed that wind had already damaged some of the roofing sheets used on completed sections of the buildings, raising concerns about the quality and durability of the materials and workmanship.

The team also sought explanations for the non-commencement of several components of the project, despite the contracts reportedly having been awarded since 2024.

The affected contractors and consultants include M/s Gozcon Investment, responsible for electricity works; M/s Blue Sea Investment Limited, handling road and drainage infrastructure; M/s Goodnews Creative Ideas Limited, also handling road and drainage works; and M/s Ecosphere Consulting Limited, engaged as consultant for the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment of the Renewed Hope Estate project in Delta State.

The representative of the Controller, Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development, Delta State, Uche Nwati, was invited to provide clarification on the status of the project and the reasons for the limited progress recorded.

Nwati attributed some of the challenges to what he described as inadequate feasibility studies conducted before the contracts were awarded. He also expressed dissatisfaction with the level of work executed at the project site.

The FRC verification team stressed the importance of ensuring that contractors engaged for Federal Government projects deliver according to approved specifications, timelines and quality standards, particularly on projects designed to provide critical social infrastructure to Nigerians.

FRC is currently undergoing physical verification of select Federal Government projects across the South-south geopolitical zone, aimed at assessing project implementation, value for money and compliance with approved standards and specifications.

World.title: NDDC Director Takes Over As ISMNC Rivers Chair
World.content:
. Pledges results-driven leadership

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

Director of Planning, Research and Statistics at the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), Dr Patterson Ogon, has assumed office as Chairman of the Rivers State Chapter of the Institute of Strategic Management of Nigeria (ISMNC), pledging to promote professional excellence, ethical leadership and measurable results.

Ogon formally took over the chapter’s administrative affairs following a handover ceremony held at the weekend in Port Harcourt, after his election to the position.

Speaking at the chapter’s inaugural meeting, swearing-in ceremony and handover of administrative responsibilities, the new chairman said his administration would consolidate the achievements of his predecessors while strengthening the institute’s role in professional development and strategic leadership.

He said the chapter would serve as a platform for strategic thinking, intellectual development, mentorship and collaboration, stressing that membership must offer tangible opportunities for learning, networking and professional growth.

“Strategy must translate into practical outcomes. Every programme and initiative undertaken by this chapter must have clear objectives, create demonstrable value and deliver measurable results,” Ogon said.

He identified continuous professional development as a major priority, noting that technological advancement, artificial intelligence, changing economic realities and evolving leadership expectations had made adaptability essential for professionals.

According to him, his administration will promote seminars, workshops and knowledge-sharing engagements while strengthening mentorship and intergenerational learning to combine the experience of established professionals with the innovative ideas and technological awareness of younger members.

Ogon also pledged to promote transparency, accountability and professional ethics, assuring members that the chapter’s resources would be managed prudently in their collective interest.

He called for stronger collaboration among members, state chapters, regional structures and the institute’s national leadership, urging professionals to contribute their expertise and opportunities towards advancing the organisation.

The National President and Chairman-in-Council of ISMNC, Ndudi Enebeli, welcomed the leadership transition, describing the Rivers State chapter as particularly significant to him.

Enebeli, however, expressed concern over growing apathy among members of professional bodies in Rivers State, challenging the new executive to develop strategies to encourage participation and re-engage inactive members.

He urged members to see the institute as a platform for continuous learning rather than participating only when specific programmes offered immediate personal benefits.

“Communication, cooperation and collaboration are essential elements of successful leadership and teamwork,” he said, while encouraging the outgoing executive to mentor and support the new leadership.

Enebeli also commended the Rivers chapter’s contributions to the institute’s national leadership, noting that it had produced the national president and had been recognised as the institute’s best-performing chapter in successive periods.

Earlier, a former chairman, Nathan Excellence, thanked members of his executive committee for their support during approximately two years in office.

Excellence said his administration was handing over a more structured institute with improved capacity to deliver on its objectives, expressing confidence that the new leadership would consolidate the gains recorded and advance the chapter’s growth.

World.title: NCWS Demands Urgent Action Against Child Marriage
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

More than 24 million Nigerian women and girls alive today were married before their 18th birthday, the National Council of Women’s Societies (NCWS) has warned, demanding urgent action to end child marriage.

In a statement on Sunday to mark the International Day of the Girl Child, the council said Nigeria, which is among countries with the highest numbers of child brides globally, cannot meet its 2030 deadline to end the practice without funded interventions and enforcement of the law.

The NCWS, under the theme ‘End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights,’ cited UNICEF figures and the 2023-2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey, which showed 33.4 per cent of women aged 20-24 were married before 18, with prevalence approaching 50 per cent in the North-east and North-west.

Its National President, Princess Edna Azura, described child marriage as a national development crisis, not a private family matter.

The council said poverty is a major driver, with girls from poor households far more likely to marry in adolescence. It warned of severe health consequences such as eclampsia, infections, obstetric fistula, prematurity and low birth weight, as well as lifelong loss of education and economic opportunities.

It cited about 7.6 million out-of-school girls nationwide, noting that women without formal education marry at a median age of 16.6 years compared to 21.7 years for those who complete secondary education.

According to the council, investing $114 million in out-of-school girls in two northern states alone could generate $2.5 billion (about N3.6 trillion) in economic benefits, based on a 2025 study by UNICEF and the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs.

The NCWS said despite all 36 states adopting the Child Rights Act, implementation remains weak.

It demanded enforcement of Section 21 of the Act, which sets 18 as the minimum age of marriage, and called on the National Assembly to review Section 29(4)(b) of the Constitution which deems a married woman to be of full age.

It also called for free birth registration, compulsory registration of all marriages with age verification, training for police, prosecutors, judges and customary and Sharia court officials and functional family courts.

The council outlined an eight-point action plan including enforcement of the marriage age, safe completion of secondary education for girls, school feeding, conditional cash transfers, menstrual hygiene support, recruitment of female teachers, second-chance education for married girls and young mothers, targeted financial assistance for poor households, and funded child protection desks, helplines, safe shelters and adolescent-friendly healthcare.

It urged traditional rulers, imams and pastors to promote later marriage and called for release of funds for the Costed National Action Plan to End Child Marriage with dedicated budget lines and annual public reporting.

“A girl’s childhood is not ours to give away,” Azura said, urging government, families and communities to protect girls’ health and allow them to determine their futures.

World.title: Got eight hours of sleep, but still tired?
World.content:
Scientists found why we might still feel tired even after getting enough sleep. Image via Pexels

You went to bed at a decent time and got eight hours of sleep. So why do you still feel exhausted even though you are getting enough sleep?

New research suggests that sleep quality may matter as much as sleep duration, with your bedroom environment potentially playing a role in your sleep quality.

Your bedroom could be affecting your sleep quality

Researchers at Penn State analysed data from 372 young adults, average age 22, who tracked their sleep for 14 days. They published the results in Sleep Health.



Participants reported whether light, noise or temperature disrupted their sleep. They also wore wrist sensors to objectively measure aspects of their sleep.

The findings suggest that bedrooms perceived as too bright, too hot or too noisy were associated with poorer sleep quality, even though these disturbances did not appear to reduce the total amount of sleep participants got.

Too bright, too hot or too noisy?

Each environmental factor affected sleep differently. When participants considered their bedrooms too bright, they tended to fall asleep later, experience poorer sleep quality and spend more time awake during the night.



Excessive heat and noise were also associated with poorer sleep quality, according to the researchers.

Noise can be particularly disruptive because parts of the brain remain alert to the surroundings during sleep, explained study co-author Orfeu Buxton, a professor of biobehavioral health at Penn State. Interestingly, a bedroom being too cold had no measurable effect in the objective sleep data.

The researchers also noted that what feels too noisy or uncomfortable for one person might not bother someone else. Rather than measuring specific noise levels, temperatures or brightness, they focused on how participants perceived their sleeping environments.



Why eight hours might not be enough

Sleep quality involves more than the number of hours spent in bed. How quickly you fall asleep, how often you wake up and how long you remain awake during the night all matter.

The researchers suggested that young adults might compensate for disrupted nights by sleeping in, potentially explaining why their sleep quality suffered without a reduction in total sleep duration. However, further research is needed.

Healthy sleep habits matter at other stages of life, too. Research has also explored the relationship between teenagers’ sleep patterns and mental health, including a weekend sleep habit linked to depression risk in teenagers.



Could simple changes help improve your sleep quality

The researchers suggest that small adjustments could help people who cannot fully control their sleeping environments.

Earplugs or noise-cancelling devices may help reduce unwanted noise, while sleep masks or blackout curtains can block excess light. Keeping your room comfortable during hot weather may also be worth prioritising.

The study focused on young adults and identified associations rather than proving that environmental changes directly improve sleep. Nevertheless, it highlights that getting enough hours in bed does not necessarily mean getting good-quality sleep.

World.title: Another English Premier League club targets Bafana Bafana star
World.content:
The 22-year-old Bafana Bafana star stormed into the Scottish Premiership with the Player of the Month award. The accolade follows after it was reported that several clubs in England, Spain and Italy have taken note of his talent.

A subsequent report revealed that Brentford were the English club setting sights on Makhanya.

BAFANA BAFANA STAR OLWETHU MAKHANYA ATTRACTS MORE INTEREST FROM ENGLAND

According to the Turkish transfer report Ekrem Kanur, English Premier League side Sunderland sent scouts to watch Makhanya in the Scottish Premier League this past weekend.



Makhanya’s award comes after an impressive September for Rangers, during which the club won all five of their fixtures, including four Scottish Premiership matches.

“I am really proud to receive this award, and I’d like to thank my teammates and all the staff for their support,” he told RangersTV. “They have helped me settle in and feel part of the group and that makes a big difference when you come to a new club.

The Bafana Bafana central defender made an immediate impact following his July move from Philadelphia Union to Rangers. Makhanya had started all six of his league appearances, playing 540 minutes and helping Rangers keep four clean sheets. He had completed 323 passes with an 85.2% accuracy rate and recorded a 7.46 match rating.

His defensive statistics were equally impressive. Across his first five matches, he recorded 20 clearances, four blocks and five interceptions. His clearance tally later increased to 24.

Makhanya began his career in the Marumo Gallants reserve team before joining Stellenbosch FC. He later moved to the USA to play for Philadelphia Union before securing his move to Rangers.

Meanwhile, Rangers are currently second in the Scottish Premiership with two points adrift leaders and fierce rivals Celtic. Coming up next is a trip to Dundee on Saturday 17 October at 21:00.

World.title: Presidency says Jacob Zuma’s health status must remain private
World.content:
Minister in the Presidency Khumbudzo Ntshavheni says only the doctors treating former president Jacob Zuma can comment authoritatively on his health following his hospitalisation.

Zuma was admitted to Netcare St Anne’s Hospital in Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, earlier this week after he reportedly fell ill after an uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party event in Msinga.

In South Africa, the sitting president and former heads of state receive medical care through the South African National Defence Force (SANDF) at 1 Military Health Hospital in Pretoria, the country’s administrative capital. However, media reports suggest that the 84-year-old’s condition is critical and that airlifting him to Pretoria has been ruled out.



PRESIDENCY WEIGHS IN ON JACOB ZUMA’S HEALTH

There has been speculation regarding the former President’s health, however, his party maintained that he was admitted for a routine check up he does twice a year. It added that he is well and in good spirits.

Speaking during a media briefing in Pretoria on Sunday, 11 October, Ntshavheni said the MK Party leader was under the care of a surgeon-general of the SANDF.

“As part of ethical requirements, it is only his medical doctors that can pronounce on his health status and his condition,” she said.

“So, there’s nobody who must continuously be asking us whether we must comment about his health status. He is being treated by the doctors, and the president has also assigned the surgeon-general to lead that process, and therefore we must leave those questions to the medical team, the family and President Zuma. You should know it’s a violation of privacy. The fact that a person holds a particular position in society does not entitle us to violate his privacy,” Ntshavheni said.

RAMAPHOSA WISHES HIS PREDECESSOR A SPEEDY RECOVERY

Following reports on Jacob Zuma’s health, President Cyril Ramaphosa wished his predecessor a speedy recovery.

“President Zuma has not been well and he is now being treated by doctors. The surgeon-general of our defence force has been well briefed and we wish President Zuma well. We wish him a very quick recovery, we want him to be well and up continuing to serve the people of South Africa in whichever way,” Ramaphosa said.

World.title: 'Everything is falling apart,' EFF calls for accountability in eThekwini.
World.content:
DURBAN - The Economic Freedom Fighters' (EFF) eThekwini mayoral candidate Hlengiwe Mkhaliphi says her party will prioritise the people.

Mkhaliphi spoke at the We The Nation Elections 2026 debate at Mangosuthu University of Technology in Umlazi on Sunday.

She lamented failures in municipal service delivery.

‘Everything is falling apart in eThekwini,’ she explained.

Mkhaliphi also accused the current leadership of failing to communicate with residents.

‘We need a mayor that loves people, loves accountability and will interact with people to solve the problem.’

Mkhaliphi wants a Metro that is transparent about the reasons for water problems.

‘They are not explaining to the community why there has been no water for eight years,’ she says.

Mkhaliphi says that in her party's first 100 days, they will address the water billing system, debt in the City, and the water crisis.

World.title: ANC a no-show at election debate
World.content:
DURBAN - ANC eThekwini mayoral candidate Cyril Xaba was a no-show at the We The Nation Elections 2026 debate at the Mangosuthu University of Technology in Umlazi on Sunday.

Mayoral candidates from the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), Democratic Alliance (DA), Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP), and uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MK Party) attended the special broadcast. Independent candidates were also present.

It is unclear why Xaba and other party members failed to arrive.

Mayor Xaba is the incumbent. He runs a Metro where residents continue to voice displeasure at the state of service delivery.

The Auditor-General noted R4.4-billion in irregular expenditure in 2024/2025.

World.title: DA promises R10bn in eThekwini water restoration
World.content:
DURBAN - The Democratic Alliance's eThekwini mayoral candidate Haniff Hoosen says the party will work towards putting R10-billion towards the City's water infrastructure should they take control of the Metro.

'We have a serious problem in the ANC over the last 20 years,' Hoosen said.

'They have not invested in the water infrastructure, and that is why we have 13,000 active water leaks throughout the City,' he explained.

The DA has promised to address water losses that run at 65%. An additional R6-billion is needed to fix ageing wastewater treatment plants.

The Auditor-General noted R4.4-billion in irregular expenditure in 2024/25.

Hoosen says they will start replacing the municipality's pipes and repairing every leak. He wants to do away with water trucks.

'We cannot continue like this,' he said.

World.title: 'If it's broken, fix it', IFP promise better services for eThekwini
World.content:
DURBAN - We need to fix what is broken, says Inkatha Freedom Party eThekwini mayoral candidate, Mkhuleko Hlengwa.

'Our approach is the broken window approach,' he says.

'If it is broken, fix it now," he adds. Hlengwa was speaking at the We The Nation Election Debate at the Mangosuthu University of Technology.

Over 65% of the metro’s treated water is lost to leaks before it reaches a tap. It’s believed an additional R6-billion is needed to fix its ageing wastewater treatment plants.

The Auditor-General noted R4.4-billion in irregular expenditure in the last financial year. In addition, over 2,300 murders were recorded in a single year. Inanda, Umlazi and KwaMashu are among the country's deadliest policing precincts.

Hlengwa says the City's water crisis needs government as a collective and society as a whole.

'We are going to constitute a Mayoral Water Crisis Committee to join civil society, academia and others to provide us with the necessary skills,' he says.

Hlengwa says water provision remains a priority for the IFP.

World.title: 109 migrants dead, 116 missing in boat wreck off Djibouti: UN
World.content:
DJIBOUTI - At least 109 migrants died, including 15 children, and 116 went missing when a boat sank off the shores of Djibouti on the night of October 8-9, a UN agency said Sunday.

Survivors said the vessel, which was carrying 305 people from Djibouti to Yemen, capsized north of the Djibouti town of Obock, according to a statement from the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

"Survivors told me that the boat started to sink backwards as soon as they got in it," Alexandre Coissac, IOM chief of mission in Djibouti, told AFP.

"This is a devastating loss of life," he said earlier in the statement.

"Our thoughts are with the survivors and the families who have lost loved ones or remain without news of their relatives."

Coissac said IOM teams were on the ground alongside Djiboutian authorities to provide emergency aid.

"This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities" by trying to cross the Bab al-Mandeb Strait to Yemen and then reach Gulf countries.

Among the 109 bodies recovered were 52 men, 42 women and 15 children, nine girls and six boys, the statement said.

More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals.

"Poverty, insecurity and the growing impacts of climate change drive many to undertake this journey, despite mounting instability across the Middle East," the IOM said.

- Perilous Yemen route -

The IOM said it was assisting 64 survivors at a migrant centre in Obock.

"Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations as fears grow for those still missing."

It said that 178,000 people had arrived in Djibouti from Ethiopia from January to October this year.

Since September 10, the IOM detected more than 20,000 crossings to Djibouti from Ethiopia, despite a surge in conflict in Yemen.

The country is stricken by fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Tehran-backed Houthi rebels, who have joined in the regional conflict involving the US and its allies against Iran.

Coissac said 150 of the people on the boat that sank off Djibouti had previously been turned back from Yemen but had attempted the crossing again.

He said he had also spoken to one survivor of the wreck who came from the Tigray region of northern Ethiopia, where rebels are battling the federal government in a recent flare-up of violence.

In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the sea route to Yemen and the number attempting the journey increased by 18 percent, the IOM said.

A shipwreck in March 2026 left nine people dead and 45 missing.

IOM spokesman Kennedy Omondi Okoth told AFP this week that most of the people attempting the journey were from Ethiopia or Somalia.

He said many of them were ending up stuck in Djibouti.

The IOM urged "donors and partners to strengthen support for Djibouti's response, including search and rescue operations and life-saving assistance".

World.title: Government eyes supervisory order on asylum ruling
World.content:
PRETORIA - Home Affairs needs more time to prepare for the implementation of the Constitutional Court’s asylum ruling.

Government has said the department needs to strengthen its systems, staff and processing capacity before the judgment can be fully implemented.

Justice Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi said government may ask the court for a supervisory order to oversee the process.

"Following a detailed legal consultation, we have been duly advised that government can approach the courts to seek a supervisory order in this regard. A supervisory order in practical terms would enable the court to retain oversight of the implementation process and provide guidance on how the order should be operationalized.

“Such an order may also include a suspension period to allow the Department of Foreign Affairs the necessary time to develop and strengthen administrative, human resource, infrastructure, and processing capacity required to implement the judgment effectively and sustainably.

“We believe that this approach represents a responsible and lawful mechanism to ensure that constitutional obligations are fulfilled in a manner that is orderly, practical and in the public interest. It will allow government to avoid administrative disruption while ensuring that the rights recognized by the court are progressively and meaningfully realized.”

World.title: All systems go for matric exams
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Basic Education Department has put plans in place to ensure this year’s matric exams run without disruption.

Minister Siviwe Gwarube said strict quality control measures and a zero-tolerance for examination irregularities will be enforced.

“This year we will have a network of around 7,100 examination centers and to ensure a secure environment, have audited an entire network and implemented risk-based monitoring approach, directing our supervision and resources exactly to where they are needed most.

“I want to assure the public that the setting, the moderation, the quality assurance, and all the examination materials are complete. All question papers and examination instruments have been rigorously reviewed by the DBE and have been approved by UMALUSI.

“Crucially, learning from the past challenges, have significantly strengthened our security controls of the entire production and distribution chain. Through the district vetting and examination officials and close collaboration with national and provincial law enforcement structures, we are safeguarding examination materials very closely.

“We have established 189 marking centers, successfully recruiting 51,104 qualified and experienced education markers to mark our scripts. We will apply a standardized national approach to marking, underpinned by strict quality control processes strengthened and the moderation of school-based assessment.

“Let me be clear; the DBE is taking a proactive, zero-tolerance approach to examination irregularities. The candidate and parent pledge agreements to instill a culture of integrity to our young ones and 24-hour examination hotline which is active for the public to report any and all suspicious activity. Furthermore, we have robust contingency plans in place to manage operational challenges including severe weather conditions, community disruptions, because we want no learner to be disadvantaged.”
